title: Bridging Segmented Markets: the Role of Active Investors
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Bridging Segmented Markets: the Role of Active Investors
detail.abstract: This paper examines how active mutual fund and ETF investors facilitate information transmission between the stock and corporate bond markets. I show that changes in active holdings and active cross-asset ownership predict future returns, while passive flows do not. More importantly, active investors enhance cross-market informational efficiency by reducing the predictability of bond returns from lagged stock returns. The effect of information coordination through active cross-asset ownership is stronger for investment-grade firms, where baseline market segmentation is greater and the benefits of information coordination are higher. The mitigation of selling frictions through higher active holdings is more pronounced during periods of adverse market conditions, where short-sale constraints are more likely to impede price discovery. Furthermore, a higher active ratio in ownership and a higher active ratio in cross-asset holdings are associated with stronger return comovement between a firm's stock and bond, reflecting greater integration between the two markets. These results highlight the importance of active management in enhancing cross-asset price discovery and market integration.

title: Venture waqf in a circular economy

detail.title: Venture waqf in a circular economy
detail.abstract: Purpose-This paper aims to enhance the impact of incorporated waqf institutions by blending their resources to promote responsible small businesses that are inclusive of human development, service to society and preservation of ecological environment and other species. This is expected to shift the paradigm of businesses from the current waste-oriented linear economy to ideally a zero-waste circular economy. Design/methodology/approach-This is an analytical study building on the experience of European Venture Philanthropy Organizations (VPOs) that work with the primary objective of making impactful businesses successful, with capital protection and return on investment being of secondary concern. This paper suggests an incorporated institutional design that blends resources for promoting responsible businesses using a new hybrid financial mechanism, namely, equity-at-default (EaD) to replace collateral and foreclosure requirements with responsibility and compassion. Findings-The research calls for changing the business paradigm from linear to circular, an incorporated institutional framework for venture waqf, purpose of the waqf to make impactful small businesses successful and designing a financial contract to loan in favor of responsible businesses that convert to equity stake for the waqf in case of default (EaD) replacing collateral and foreclosure requirements. Research limitations/implications-This is a theoretical study motivated by the success of VPOs but assigns a new role to waqf institutions. Furthermore, the incorporated nature of waqf is a new idea and EaD is a new mechanism. Being new, these ideas have the risk of not being implemented. However, the broader message that waqf shall promote businesses that are inclusive of ecological concerns is applicable. Practical implications-The paper has a significant practical implication to transform the responsibility and consciousness of businesses. Waqf is fundamentally a compassionate institution, and it must enhance the responsibility of businesses to become more inclusive of the environment and other species. It should also become more compassionate toward businesses that are in distress and default. In this sense, the paper tries to internalize compassion in financial contracting that can potentially change the architecture of lending. Social implications-Altering businesses' mindset from a waste-driven extractive linear economy to inclusive circular economy has a tremendous transformative role. This will have implications for enhancing business consciousness and responsibility. As poverty is a phenomenon of state of mind, changing the society's state of thought in Muslim communities is expected to have basic positive implications. Entrepreneurs with a new mindset can have far-reaching positive impacts on society. Originality/value-The paper offers potentially innovative perspectives in four key areas and blends the different resources in an incorporated waqf that makes responsible entrepreneurs assume a partnership role in times of distress through EaD. Furthermore, the integration of compassion in financial contracting could have better implications for return on investment as well. The ideal state of an economy is where waste is turned into wealth and well-being is something that all policymakers must keep on the top of their agendas.

title: Do Employees Value the Right to Sue Their Employer?
affiliations: Washington University in Saint Louis, John M. Olin Business School, Students and Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: Do Employees Value the Right to Sue Their Employer?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: Study was approved by IRB
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: The use of mandatory Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) clauses, which limit employees' ability to resolve labor disputes through the judicial system, has grown rapidly in recent decades. Despite their prevalence, little is known about how these clauses influence employee decision-making and perceived outcomes, particularly in the context of job selection. We begin by documenting trends in the prevalence and consequences of ADR clauses. Using a revealed preference survey experiment, we estimate that workers are willing to forgo 2.2% of their salary to avoid ADR clauses. Willingness to pay to avoid these clauses is higher for members of protected groups, such as women (3.5%) and Black employees (4.1%). We also find that risk aversion and prior litigation experience meaningfully shape these preferences. Finally, employees appear inattentive to ADR clauses, with willingness to pay more than doubles when these clauses are made more salient.

title: Tractable Conditions for Stochastic Arbitrage in Index Options: Theory and Evidence
affiliations: Graduate School of Business of Nazarbayev University and

detail.title: Tractable Conditions for Stochastic Arbitrage in Index Options: Theory and Evidence
detail.abstract: This study develops and applies tractable conditions for stochastic arbitrage in equity index options. The conditions, derived from the dual formulation of asset pricing restrictions, take the form of a relatively small set of linear inequalities and can incorporate bid-ask spreads and potential portfolio constraints. Because return distributions vary across volatility regimes, the inequalities must be tested conditionally, as unconditional tests cannot establish market inefficiency. Using the proposed arbitrage conditions and statistical dominance tests, we reexamine efficiency in one-month S&P 500 index options. Out-of-sample performance analysis points at arbitrage opportunities in high-volatility regimes, predominantly in the form of call front spreads. These opportunities often remain undetected unless both the volatility dependence of the market risk premium and the negative conditional skewness of index returns are taken into account. When volatility is low to moderate, no significant arbitrage opportunities are detected, consistent with higher pricing efficiency.

title: Challenges and Strategies in Post-Editing English into Arabic Neural Machine Translations of Movie Subtitles
affiliations: Mustansiriyah University

detail.title: Challenges and Strategies in Post-Editing English into Arabic Neural Machine Translations of Movie Subtitles
detail.abstract: This study investigates the challenges and strategies involved in post-editing (PE) Neural Machine Translation (NMT) subtitles for the Netflix movie La La Land from English to Arabic, utilizing Gottlieb's ten subtitling strategies. By adopting a descriptive-qualitative approach, this study identified issues related to linguistic fidelity, cultural adaptation, and technical constraints. The findings also revealed an enhanced understanding of audiovisual translation workflows, emphasizing the role of human expertise in refining machine-generated outputs. Among these, paraphrasing was the most frequently used strategy as many dialogues required localization and modification to enhance clarity for an Arabic audience. In contrast, transcription, cultural substitution, and deletion were employed less often. The study highlights the importance of human expertise in refining machine-generated output and offers recommendations for optimizing Arabic subtitle PE in NMT environments.

title: Central banks' financial stability orientation and bank risk-taking
affiliations: Universitas Indonesia and Universitas Indonesia

detail.title: Central banks' financial stability orientation and bank risk-taking

declarations.ethicsApproval: The author confirms that there are no known conflicts of interest associated with this publication and there has been no significant financial support for this work that could have influenced its outcome.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was funded by Bank Indonesia Research Grant program.

detail.abstract: Existing literature provides inconclusive theoretical predictions regarding whether central banks' monetary policy should address financial stability or not. We therefore empirically evaluate the effect of central banks' financial stability orientation ("leaning against the wind") on bank risk-taking. Our baseline results from a crosscountry bank-level panel data suggest that higher central banks' financial stability orientation significantly reduces bank risk-taking. Further investigation shows that monetary policy aimed for financial stability complements macroprudential policy in reducing bank risk-taking, particularly during macroprudential policy tightening. These results offer novel insights into the effect of central bank's monetary policy on bank stability and provides empirical evidence to prior theoretical works.

title: Defusing the social minefield of gold sites in Kamituga, South Kivu. From legal pluralism to the re-making of institutions?
affiliations: Université Catholique de Bukavu,  and University of Antwerp

detail.title: Defusing the social minefield of gold sites in Kamituga, South Kivu. From legal pluralism to the re-making of institutions?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Permission to conduct the research was granted by the University of Antwerp’s Ethics Committee for the Social Sciences and Humanities (file nr. SHW_15_06), by the Congolese Ministry of Mines, by SAESSCAM (the Congolese public Service for Assistance to Artisanal and Small-Scale mining) and by the local authorities in Kamituga.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was funded by FWO – Research Foundation Flanders (grant numbers 1517614N & 11Q2816N), and by CEGEMI – Centre d'Expertise en Gestion Minière

detail.abstract: DRC's 2002 Mining Code has attracted Large-Scale Mining (LSM) through favorable fiscal conditions, but is detrimental to Artisanal and Small-scale Mining (ASM). The Code specifies that ASM should take place in Artisanal Exploitation Zones (AEZ), but far too few AEZ were created to accommodate the large number of artisanal miners. This has triggered an explosive situation, as many artisanal miners operate in mining concessions granted to LSM companies. While LSM companies justify their operations referring to statutory law, miners claim traditional rights to the land. We study how this situation of legal pluralism plays out in Kamituga, a gold mining area in South-Kivu. To what extent do the artisanal miners and the LSM company stick to their opposing frames of reference? To what extent do they look for compromises? Can these compromises give way to the re-making of institutions?

title: An Analytical Study of Public and Private Sector Bank Employees with Respect to Work Culture and Employee Morale
affiliations: Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj Nagpur University

detail.title: An Analytical Study of Public and Private Sector Bank Employees with Respect to Work Culture and Employee Morale
detail.abstract: Appropriate work culture can boost the morale of the people to a large extent resulting in intrinsic satisfaction for the employees. It also helps in improving the productivity, creating healthy organizational climate and all round harmony in the organization. Similarly when the morale is high it can also positively make a substantial impact on the work culture. The purpose of this study was compare work culture and morale of public and private sector bank employees of Nagpur city. Researchers have chosen six different parameters each of work culture and morale for this study. The relevant data was collected from public and private sector banks of Nagpur city using a structured questionnaire. It was concluded that there are significant differences in the opinion of the employees of public and private sector banks in Nagpur city.

title: Do Farmers Know Their Safety Net? Awareness and Satisfaction with Crop Insurance in Coastal Odisha
affiliations: Rama Devi Women's University and Rama Devi Women's University

detail.title: Do Farmers Know Their Safety Net? Awareness and Satisfaction with Crop Insurance in Coastal Odisha

publicationDetails.detailsText: EPRA International Journal of Agriculture and Rural Economic Research, 0[10.36713/epra24293]

detail.abstract: Agriculture in coastal Odisha remains highly vulnerable to monsoon rainfall variability, making crop insurance a critical tool for risk management. This study examines whether farmers are aware of and satisfied with crop insurance, focusing on the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), which is the sole crop insurance scheme implemented in the state. Primary data were collected from 407 paddy cultivators across seven coastal districts of Odisha. A multi-stage purposive sampling approach was used to select districts and villages, and respondents were drawn by simple random sampling from village lists. Awareness was measured with dichotomous and multiple-response items, while satisfaction was assessed through a multi-item Likert scale (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.910; KMO = 0.852). Analysis comprised descriptive statistics, cross-tabulations and Chi-square tests to examine associations with socio-economic characteristics. Findings reveal that although awareness is fairly widespread, satisfaction levels present a sharper divide. While farmers are generally satisfied with premiums and payment modes, dissatisfaction is concentrated around claim settlement, coverage adequacy, and service responsiveness. The results confirm that socio-economic disparities significantly influence both awareness and satisfaction, indicating that crop insurance has yet to evolve into an equitable and trusted safety net. Thus, while crop insurance provides a framework for managing rainfall risk, for many farmers in coastal Odisha the promise of a reliable safety net remains only partially realized because operational and informational gaps limit trust and effective use.

title: DEVELOPMENTAL STATE AND COLOMBIAN CONSTITUTIONAL PRINCIPLES Developmental State and Constitutional Principles
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: DEVELOPMENTAL STATE AND COLOMBIAN CONSTITUTIONAL PRINCIPLES Developmental State and Constitutional Principles
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the relationship between Joseph Stiglitz's analytical framework for the developmental state and the fundamental principles enshrined in Title I of the 1991 Colombian Constitution. It examines whether these constitutional articles provide institutional mechanisms to correct market failures, promote a pragmatic balance of development, and strengthen both the hard (physical) and soft (educational, financial, and technological) infrastructure necessary for sustained and equitable growth. It also assesses whether the Colombian state, in its constitutional configuration, fosters deliberate public policies of redistribution and equality that contribute to rewriting the rules of the market economy, expanding the competitiveness and bargaining power of workers.

title: The Rise of Specialized Financial Products
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis - Department of Economics, Northwestern University and Washington University in St. Louis

detail.title: The Rise of Specialized Financial Products
detail.abstract: The variety of financial products available for firms to raise funds has expanded rapidly in recent decades. This paper studies the role of innovations that introduce specialized financial products using a combination of granular data and a parsimonious model of security issuance. We present three key findings. First, differential product adoption across firms explains most of the observed variation in the amounts of funds raised. Second, firms that adopt new products are more successful in raising funds. Third, the funds raised from new financial products are often sourced from numerous highly specialized products, each used by only a few firms.

title: From Mortgages to Meadows: Leveraging Ecopoints to protect Biodiversity
affiliations: Swiss National Bank - Financial Stability

detail.title: From Mortgages to Meadows: Leveraging Ecopoints to protect Biodiversity
detail.abstract: Biodiversity has been declining dramatically over the last few decades. Financing and investment decisions can impact biodiversity, but currently take little account of their effect on it. Against this backdrop we evaluate the possibility of aligning financial flows with biodiversity goals. First, we identify mortgage provision as an essential financial flow that can also have an impact on biodiversity. Second, we show that it is difficult to measure biodiversity globally because comparable metrics and data are not readily available, so a national or regional perspective is needed-in contrast to for example carbon emission metrics in the context of climate change. In order to then take a national perspective, we focus on Germany as a developed country because the literature has thus far examined only emerging and developing countries. Finally, we show how an existing biodiversity conservation metric, the Ecopoints, can be leveraged and integrated in mortgage lending to help protect biodiversity in Germany.

title: Advancing GPS Spoofing Detection for Autonomous Vehicles through Deep Learning and Hybrid Architectures
affiliations: Coastline Community College, Coastline College and Coastline Community College

detail.title: Advancing GPS Spoofing Detection for Autonomous Vehicles through Deep Learning and Hybrid Architectures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There were no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that could influence the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human subjects were used in the study.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was not a funded project.

detail.abstract: This research investigates the evolving threat of GPS spoofing within Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) and its implications for autonomous vehicle (AV) navigation. Through a comprehensive comparative analysis of three leading deep learning models Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and Transformer architectures, the study evaluates each model's capacity for detecting spoofed signals under dynamic, real-world conditions. Civilian GPS signals, lacking encryption and authentication, remain highly vulnerable to adversarial manipulation, posing systemic risks to transportation, defense, and industrial infrastructures. By synthesizing literature across GNSS security, machine learning, and cyber-physical system resilience, this research demonstrates that hybridized deep learning models, particularly Transformer-CNN-LSTM frameworks, achieve superior detection accuracy (≥95-99%) with minimal false alarm rates. The findings underscore the necessity of integrating multi-sensor fusion, explainable AI (XAI), and edge computing for real-time spoofing mitigation. Ultimately, the study provides a benchmark for developing adaptive, scalable, and trustworthy GPS spoofing detection systems that align with NIST cybersecurity frameworks and ensure operational integrity for next-generation autonomous vehicles.

title: Reimagining Legal Education Through Purpose-Built GPTs: A Suite of AI Tutors for Critical Thinking and Authentic Practice
affiliations: Queensland University of Technology - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Reimagining Legal Education Through Purpose-Built GPTs: A Suite of AI Tutors for Critical Thinking and Authentic Practice

contentType.other: Draft paper setting out methodology for developing GPTs for legal education

detail.abstract: Law Schools face many pressures, including reduced depth of critical engagement, the increased need for practice-ready communication, and the rapid deployment of generative AI across education and legal work. This paper introduces a suite of purpose-built GPTs for legal education designed to restore rigour while scaling up feedback and access for students. Each system addresses a specific pedagogical deficit, from making reasoning structures visible, to rehearsing legal memorandum writing, to simulating commercial practice. In this paper, I explain the design methodology and offer narrative descriptions of how each tool works in practice and what impact it is intended to have on learning.

title: FOG Business Model: A Framework for Identifying Legal-but-Misleading Commercial Practices
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: FOG Business Model: A Framework for Identifying Legal-but-Misleading Commercial Practices

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author, Shateer Shah, declares no conflicts of interest related to this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No proprietary or external datasets were generated or analyzed for this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any financial support from a funding agency, commercial entity, or not-for-profit organization.

detail.abstract: Background: Modern commercial landscapes feature numerous business models that operate within legal boundaries while systematically disadvantaging most participants through false promises and asymmetric outcomes. These practices span diverse sectors from multi-level marketing to cryptocurrency schemes. Objective: This study introduces the FOG (Fake Opportunity Guarantee) business model framework—a novel taxonomy for identifying and analyzing legal-but-misleading commercial practices that promise guaranteed opportunities while delivering losses for the majority of participants. Methods: We developed an 8-point detection checklist through analysis of common deceptive business patterns and validated it against established case studies across multiple industries. The framework was tested using representative examples from timeshare operations, MLM schemes, online course offerings, and cryptocurrency ventures. Case studies were selected through a structured search of regulatory filings, consumer complaint databases, and publicly available income disclosures. Two independent raters scored each case using the checklist, with discrepancies resolved through discussion. Inter-rater agreement exceeded 0.85 Cohen’s kappa. Results: The FOG framework successfully differentiated between legitimate business opportunities and exploitative models using quantifiable criteria. Businesses fulfilling 5 or more of the 8 detection points consistently demonstrated asymmetric outcomes favoring operators over participants, while those meeting 4 or fewer points showed more balanced value propositions. Sensitivity analysis varying the threshold between 4 and 6 points produced similar classifications, supporting robustness. Conclusions: The FOG business model provides a systematic approach to identifying predatory commercial practices operating in legal gray areas. This framework offers valuable insights for consumers, regulators, and researchers studying asymmetric business relationships and market manipulation tactics.

title: Measuring and Mitigating Drip Pricing Overcharge: Evidence from an Online Marketplace Experiment with a Digital Shopping Assistant
affiliations: , Yale Law School, Brooklyn Law School and Boston University - School of Law

detail.title: Measuring and Mitigating Drip Pricing Overcharge: Evidence from an Online Marketplace Experiment with a Digital Shopping Assistant
detail.abstract: We study how much drip pricing (hidden mandatory fees revealed after consumers have begun the buying process) raises prices paid for identical goods and whether an automated shopping assistant mitigates the effect. In a randomized online marketplace experiment (n = 1608) with real purchases of gift cards funded by a $15 endowment, we vary the initial and final presentation of the gift cards' prices across 33 levels and randomly assign participants to an automated assistant that flags a lower‑price identical option and links to it. Relative to transparent pricing, drip pricing increases the average price paid by up to a plateau of about 10% (maximum 13%) for the same gift cards. The assistant reduces the incidence of overpayment by 63% and substantially lowers dollars overpaid, enough to flip the seller's profit-maximizing strategy from drip pricing to transparent pricing. Participants exposed to drip pricing rate the platform as less trustworthy, even though it is the third-party seller that determines the fees. The digital assistant partially exacerbates this perception. Our findings inform policy responses to drip pricing and the value proposition of AI shopping tools.

title: AI and Post-Purchase Behavior: Personalization, Behavioral Insights, and Ethical Challenges
affiliations: Islamic Azad University and Payame Noor University

detail.title: AI and Post-Purchase Behavior: Personalization, Behavioral Insights, and Ethical Challenges

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not need ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was not funded.

detail.abstract: By personalization, predictive analytics, and recommendation systems, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing consumer behavior, particularly post-purchase behavior. To understand the multifaceted impact of AI on consumer behavior, this study examines how AI-driven technologies like recommendation systems and personalization tools influence post-purchase behaviors. We uncover key outcomes, such as satisfaction, loyalty, and dissatisfaction, through the integration of empirical research and theoretical frameworks. Although AI enhances consumer experiences through tailored recommendations and predictive insights, it also raises ethical concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, and data security. To increase consumer satisfaction and loyalty, AI systems not only personalize content but also predict and adapt to evolving preferences. However, these technologies often operate without consumers' full awareness, making it challenging to distinguish between beneficial personalization and manipulative design. The study encourages the adoption of responsible AI practices. We conclude by suggesting future studies direction that emphasize long-term effects and applications across diverse sectors.

title: Equity Premium Prediction with Shrinkage Estimation Guided by Economic Theory
affiliations: , Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU), University of Warwick - Warwick Business School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Equity Premium Prediction with Shrinkage Estimation Guided by Economic Theory

keywords: Equity premium prediction JEL codes: E5

detail.abstract: We demonstrate that economic linkages between predictors and the real economy, combined with theory-implied parameter restrictions, substantially enhance out-of-sample equity premium forecasting performance. We introduce a novel empirical Bayes (EB) framework that captures these economic relationships while accommodating theoretical constraints on predictor coefficients. Our EB methodology optimally shrinks coefficient estimates toward intermediate values between unrestricted OLS estimates and theory-implied restricted estimates. Empirical applications reveal improved forecasting performance across numerous established predictors. Using two comprehensive datasets, we document superior EB forecasting performance compared to traditional OLS methods. The improvements become particularly pronounced when implementing classic economic constraints following Campbell and Thompson (2008) and Pettenuzzo, Timmermann, and Valkanov (2014). These findings provide new insights into the crucial role of economic theory in time-series predictability and demonstrate how theory-implied parameter restrictions enhance predictive accuracy.

title: Differences in Loyalty Factors Between Ball Sports and Physical Sports
affiliations: Meiji University, Independent, Independent and Independent

detail.title: Differences in Loyalty Factors Between Ball Sports and Physical Sports
detail.abstract: As corporate sports activities gain popularity, many companies face the need for management aimed at developing the sports industry. However, little knowledge exists regarding the strengthening of sports brands. Therefore, we applied structural equation modeling to an online survey of 1,000 Japanese people (aged 20–60) engaged in ball sports and physical sports in Japan to clarify the factors that influence brand image. In ball sports, joy, health, relationships, and digital community positively influenced brand image, while accessibility had no significant effect. In physical sports, joy, health, accessibility, and digital community showed positive effects, whereas relationships had no significant effect. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, consumers have increasingly begun to enjoy consumption behaviors in digital spaces. Thus, regardless of the type of sport, practitioners should promote innovation in sports through digital transformation (DX). Practitioners should digitally enhance people's sports experiences through DX, as DX shapes a consumer experience in business.

title: Which Markets Organisation to Enhance a Transition to Natural Farming? Apples as the new Lemons in Himachal Pradesh
affiliations: Ecole des Ponts ParisTech and Dr. YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry

detail.title: Which Markets Organisation to Enhance a Transition to Natural Farming? Apples as the new Lemons in Himachal Pradesh

declarations.funderStatement: Acropics EU funded project: https://acp-initiative.com/fr/acropics/

detail.abstract: Agriculture is an important sector of the Indian economy, but smallholders face persistent environmental and economic challenges. In Himachal Pradesh, the government has initiated a transition to natural farming to reduce input use and improve sustainability. However, the market has not yet adapted to this type of production. This article examines the functioning of regulated wholesale markets (APMC/mandis) for apples and highlights a double asymmetry of information and collusive practices that undermine competitiveness. Based on field observations, it shows how different institutions influence trading practices, leaving no room for products from natural agriculture. The article then analyses public initiatives, such as various labelling systems and minimum support prices for natural products, as well as various private initiatives, notably through the implementation of targeted cooperatives. The results suggest that, although public and private interventions provide partial solutions, an integrated approach is needed to promote natural agriculture in differentiated markets, strengthen the capacities of cooperatives and enable a fair transition to sustainable food systems.

title: The Impact of Covid-19 on Consumer Behaviour and Online Shopping: The Case Study in the Developing Country
affiliations: AAB College - Faculty of Economics, AAB College - Faculty of Economics, AAB College - Faculty of Economics and AAB College - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: The Impact of Covid-19 on Consumer Behaviour and Online Shopping: The Case Study in the Developing Country
detail.abstract: The main purpose of this study is to assess the impact of the pandemic on online shopping in the case of Kosovo. Cunningham (2019) states that online shopping is an e-commerce activity that involves buying items on a seller’s website through a credit or debit card and delivering the item to your home with online shopping, customers buy items from anywhere in the world through a digital platform. The data used are primary, collected through the online questionnaire and it was distributed using social media Facebook, Instagram, and Gmail to a random sample of 500 respondents from Kosovo. We have concluded that the COVID-19 pandemic has had a positive impact on online shopping because, based on the results we have obtained, online shopping has increased during this period. Online shopping clearly shows that consumers’ attitudes and behaviors have changed rapidly, but the pandemic had not increased their confidence in online shopping. This is especially true for developed countries, where every store has its website from which to buy, and India seems to have adopted this trend very fast compared to Pakistan (Bashir, Mehboob, & Bhatti, 2015). The most demanded products besides food, and hygiene, there was a great demand for clothing, electronic and technological equipment, books, and others. Regardless of how many advantages we can have from online shopping, traditional shopping is still what Kosovar consumers prefer to practice. The paper also suggests some recommendations regarding online shopping in Kosovo.

title: Building Persuasive Stories with Emotion Sequences
affiliations: University of Toronto, University of Colorado at Boulder - Leeds School of Business and University of Colorado at Boulder - Leeds School of Business

detail.title: Building Persuasive Stories with Emotion Sequences

declarations.funderStatement: Center for Ethics and Social Responsibility (CESR) Research Fellowship, University of Colorado Boulder

detail.abstract: What types of stories are most persuasive? In this paper, we introduce a new template for categorizing story types based on the specific emotional dynamics of text, or "emotion sequences"—for example, whether a story begins fearful and ends with sadness, or vice versa. We present this as a new way to capture distinct narrative progressions that is tractable even in short-form media, and then apply this method to analyze the persuasiveness of different story types in online fundraising. Using transformer-based emotion classification tools, we measure the two-part emotion sequences of 14,000 medical fundraising pitches from GoFundMe.org and show that, among other findings, medical fundraising pitches that begin with a sad tone and end on a caring tone are significantly more likely to succeed. We then develop a simple new approach for testing the generalizability of these observational findings by using crowd-sourced, LLM-assisted rewrites to introduce particular emotion sequences to a sample of 40 randomly-selected fundraisers. We show that human-only rewrites generally fail due to skill deficits (and LLM-only rewrites can introduce salient informational changes from originals), but demonstrate that crowd-sourced, LLM-assisted rewriting offers an effective method for testing the out-of-sample application of research results by everyday online users. With this, we establish that pitches rewritten to feature our focal emotion sequences see a significant boost in perceived persuasiveness, even for some sequences associated with lower success in observational data, while placebo rewrites produce null effects. Furthermore, we show that increased identification with the protagonist of the fundraiser is the primary mechanism driving the observed effects.

title: Humour, Surrogacy and Masculinity in Imperial Blue’s Advertisements

detail.title: Humour, Surrogacy and Masculinity in Imperial Blue’s Advertisements
detail.abstract: This paper assesses campaigns of Imperial Blue's 'Men will be Men' through various communication objectives, target market and integrated marketing tools with comparisons made using its direct competitors like Royal Stag and McDowell's which highlight the distinctive usage of humor and consistent brand assets.

title: Perceived Authenticity in Paid Instagram Advertising: A Behavioral Science Approach
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Perceived Authenticity in Paid Instagram Advertising: A Behavioral Science Approach
detail.abstract: The growing prevalence of paid advertising on Instagram has raised critical questions about consumer perception, particularly the role of authenticity in shaping advertising effectiveness. While sponsored content offers brands access to highly engaged audiences, consumer skepticism toward overtly commercial messages often diminishes trust and purchase intention. This paper adopts a behavioral science perspective to examine how authenticity is constructed, perceived, and evaluated in the context of paid Instagram advertising. By integrating insights from social psychology, consumer behavior, and digital marketing research, the study explores mechanisms such as source credibility, self-congruence, and emotional resonance that influence authenticity judgments. The findings highlight that transparent disclosures, alignment between influencer and brand values, and consistency in messaging are essential in mitigating skepticism and fostering positive consumer responses. These insights offer valuable implications for advertisers, influencers, and policymakers seeking to balance commercial objectives with consumer trust in the evolving digital marketplace.

title: A Practical Guide to Business Communication (Module One)

detail.title: A Practical Guide to Business Communication (Module One)
detail.abstract: This module, A Practical Guide to Business Communication (Module One), provides a comprehensive exploration of communication as a strategic driver of organizational performance and growth. It emphasizes that communication is not merely a soft skill but a core mechanism for transmitting ideas, shaping meaning, fostering collaboration, and sustaining competitive advantage in business contexts. The document systematically examines the fundamental components of communication, sender, message, receiver, channels, and feedback, while situating them within the complexities of modern organizational structures and cultural environments. The text delineates the dual dimensions of communication: informational accuracy and relational credibility, underscoring how clarity, conciseness, and professional etiquette influence decision-making, leadership effectiveness, and customer trust. Key themes include the distinctions between formal and informal channels, the interplay of verbal and non-verbal signals, the necessity of cultural awareness in globalized environments, and the transformative role of digital technologies such as Zoom, Slack, and social media. These elements are contextualized through Drexel University case examples, making theoretical insights practical and relatable for students preparing for academic, professional, and co-op experiences. A significant contribution of the module lies in its integration of classical and contemporary models of communication. It analyzes linear, interactive, and transactional approaches alongside specialized models, including Lasswell’s, Westley and MacLean’s, and the Convergence Model. By linking theory to application, the module demonstrates how models function as diagnostic and predictive tools for resolving miscommunication, enhancing team collaboration, and aligning strategic messaging with organizational objectives. This guide frames communication as a dynamic, multimodal, and multicultural process central to leadership, teamwork, negotiation, crisis response, and organizational growth. Through its structured balance of theory, practice, and context-specific examples, it equips learners with the analytical and applied skills necessary to navigate complex business environments and to leverage communication as a strategic asset in shaping sustainable outcomes.

detail.abstract: The study is aimed to investigate the influences of identified precursors on attitude toward vlogger recommendations and purchase intention, attitude on purchase intentions, and test the mediating role of attitude between its precursors and purchase intention. The respondents were 333 Filipinos who were Facebook followers of well-known vloggers. The predictive-causal research approach and a quantitative research design was used in this paper. The direct and indirect links between the latent variables of the structural model were estimated using partial least squares. The results revealed that perceived usefulness, perceived benefits, trust, expertise, attractiveness, and attitude towards vlogger recommendations were found to be related in this study. Moreover, attitude, perceived usefulness, expertise, attractiveness, and purchase intention have significant relationships, respectively. On the other hand, the mediating effect of attitude was established between perceived usefulness, perceived benefits, trust, expertise, attractiveness, and purchase intention. As regards vlogger recommendations in particular, this study provides a fresh viewpoint on attitude as a mediator of purchase intentions in the Philippines.

title: Experiential Marketing in the Experience Economy: Insights from Kumarakom, Kerala

detail.title: Experiential Marketing in the Experience Economy: Insights from Kumarakom, Kerala

publicationDetails.detailsText: Presented at National Tribal Tourism Conference-2025 with Theme "Globalization of Tribal Heritage: Inclusive, Responsible and Sustainable Tourism".

detail.abstract: Experiential marketing, closely tied to Pine and Gilmore’s idea of the experience economy, shifts attention from selling products and services to creating meaningful, memorable experiences. In tourism, this perspective is especially relevant since destinations are primarily consumed as lived experiences rather than tangible commodities. This study applies Schmitt’s Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs) to examine how Kumarakom, a prominent backwater destination in Kerala, India, can be positioned through experiential rather than traditional marketing approaches. Using a case study design, secondary data and tourism reports were analysed to understand how SEM dimensions are reflected in Kumarakom’s cultural and adventure offerings. The Sense dimension emerges in multisensory encounters such as birdwatching at the Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary, houseboat cruises, and regional cuisines like Karemeen. Feel is fostered through the emotional pull of events such as the Nehru Trophy Boat Race and the Kumarakom Backwater Festival, which connect visitors to Kerala’s traditions. The Think dimension is evident in biodiversity explorations and guided nature walks that encourage reflection and learning, while Act experes include coconut tree climbing, toddy tapping, and traditional fishing, which invite physical participation. Finally, Relate is expressed through community-based initiatives and cultural exchanges that build social connections and belonging.The findings indicate that Kumarakom demonstrates how Schmitt’s SEM framework can be implemented in practice to design holistic “experiencescapes.” These experiences strengthen destination competitiveness, nurture tourist loyalty, and contribute to sustainable tourism development. By translating SEM theory into applied destination management, this study highlights the role of experiential marketing in creating authentic, memorable, and co-created tourism experiences.

title: Consumer Protection Laws and Application: A Case Study of Pakistan

detail.title: Consumer Protection Laws and Application: A Case Study of Pakistan

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Research Society of Pakistan, Volume 57, No.3.

detail.abstract: Generally, in most of the countries, consumer protection consists of laws and organizations designed to ensure the rights of consumers and the free flow of truthful information in the marketplace. The laws are designed to prevent business trade activities that engaged in fraud or specified unfair practices from gaining an advantage over competitors and may provide additional protection for the weak and those unable to take care of themselves. Consumer protection is linked to the idea of "consumer rights" (that consumers have various rights as consumers), and to the formation of consumer organizations, which help consumers make better choices in the market place and get help with consumer complaints. However, the consumer protection laws are new in the country and their implementation is under process. Therefore, the Consumer Courts, and sometimes in appeals before High Courts, the Hon'ble Judges give their own interpretation to the vague language of the provision of this Act, 2005. And if an order is passed in favour of a consumer at the forum of Consumer Court after a period of about two or three years litigation, an appeal is routinely filed in about 90% cases before High Court which again takes about two to three years for decision. The result is that a Consumer approaching a Consumer Court regarding a product or service, to whatever petite matter or amount involved, does not get final relief until after the lapse of five to six years period. The provisions of the Act, 2005, not only require providing speedy remedy to the consumers but their scope should also be broadened. The procedure should be further simplified till the stage, the consumer gets his right or remedy.

title: The Usage and Impact of Differentiation: Evidence from an Online EdTech Platform
affiliations: Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Marketing,  and New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business

detail.title: The Usage and Impact of Differentiation: Evidence from an Online EdTech Platform
detail.abstract: We study teachers' usage of a digital differentiation tool for reading comprehension assignments on an educational technology platform and examine how usage shapes the tool's effectiveness. Using a structural model that combines a hidden Markov framework of student ability evolution with a two-stage teacher decision process, we evaluate the usage and implementation of the differentiation tool and their impact on student performance. The analysis yields three main findings. First, observed differentiation practices offer only modest gains over no differentiation, whereas full differentiation, in which every student receives a differentiated assignment, generates substantial improvements. Second, despite this potential, real-world usage remains limited and implementation strategies differ by context: teachers in low-poverty schools tend to prioritize lower-ability students, while those in high-poverty schools more often direct differentiation toward higher-ability students. Third, platform-led interventions can narrow the gap between potential and actual impact. Reducing implementation costs increases usage but disproportionately benefits low-poverty schools, while combining cost reduction with targeted training in high-poverty schools raises usage and reduces disparities across socioeconomic groups. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for user behavior in evaluating educational technologies and show how platform interventions can unlock their full benefits.

title: Profitability of Two-Part Tariffs in Name-Your-Own-Price Markets
affiliations: University of Würzburg - Business Administration & Economics, University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) and University of Alberta - Department of Marketing, Business Economics & Law

detail.title: Profitability of Two-Part Tariffs in Name-Your-Own-Price Markets
detail.abstract: Name-Your-Own-Price (NYOP) mechanisms offer retailers a participatory and price-discriminating alternative to posted pricing, yet two-part NYOP pricing—a strategy charging a non-refundable bidding fee—remains rare despite theoretical support for improved profitability. We present results from two incentive-compatible laboratory experiments and a field experiment examining the effectiveness of this two-part NYOP mechanism and key behavioral factors moderating its profitability. We find that two-part tariffs can improve seller profitability, particularly in novel or information-poor environments. However, the optimal fee level is lower than theoretical predictions based on risk-neutral buyer models due to a robust preference inconsistency: consumers appear risk-neutral when deciding whether to participate but behave as if risk-averse when bidding. The apparent risk-aversion in bidding increases bid amounts, but it also limits the effectiveness of higher fees because it deters entry of bidders who tend to bid a lot. We also document two managerially relevant moderators of the two-part NYOP pricing strategy: both prior consumer experience with the strategy and the provision of decision aids by the retailer suppress consumer participation and reduce or even eliminate the strategy’s profitability. Finally, our field experiment shows that modest fees can improve profits in short-term sales campaigns, consistently with the findings in the laboratory. These findings suggest retailers should carefully calibrate bidding fees, considering consumer learning and decision support tools, and may find two-part NYOP mechanisms most effective as short-term promotions or membership benefits rather than permanent pricing strategies.

title: Cognitive Processing of Hashtags: How Social Cues Influence Consumer Recall and Attitude Formation
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Cognitive Processing of Hashtags: How Social Cues Influence Consumer Recall and Attitude Formation
detail.abstract: Hashtags have become an essential feature of digital communication, serving not only as categorization tools but also as cognitive cues that guide consumer interpretation and memory. This paper examines how hashtags function as social signals that influence consumer recall, attention, and attitude formation toward brands in online environments. Drawing on cognitive psychology and communication theories, the study explores how hashtags prime mental associations, enhance message salience, and shape attitudes through perceived relevance and social endorsement. Findings suggest that strategically framed hashtags can improve brand recall by triggering associative memory pathways, while socially embedded hashtags foster positive attitudes by signaling community, authenticity, and shared identity. By highlighting the cognitive underpinnings of hashtag use, this work contributes to a deeper understanding of how digital cues mediate consumer responses in an era of social media-driven marketing.

title: Sustainable Web-design: Digital Marketing Potentials

detail.title: Sustainable Web-design: Digital Marketing Potentials

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors do not have any conflicts of interest to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study has been approved by the ethics committee of the International School of Management and is listed under number K-2025-JP-14.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding has been received.

detail.abstract: The present study is motivated by the increasing ecological impact resulting from the energy consumption of the internet, i.e., the large number of websites. Sustainable web design, the reduction of data volume, the optimization and compression of website elements as well as ecological hosting, can not only reduce the ecological footprint, but also improve the technical performance and user experience of websites. Design Against this background, a mixed-methods research approach is developed combining expert interviews and a discrete choice experiment. Based on the results of a literature analysis and the expert interviews, five attributes are deduced for the design of this study's choice cards. Findings A fast loading time of websites turns out to be particularly decisive and users will perceive the company or brand and the quality of their products or services more positively. The probability of a purchase also increases. In addition, communication measures of sustainable web design practices in the form of sustainability seals, the disclosure of hosting using green electricity and the provision of transparent information about corresponding sustainability efforts also have a positive impact on users. Their use and implementation significantly increases the probability of a positive perception, quality assessment and purchase decision on the user side. Originality The stufy is the first to consider the topic of green and sustainable web design from a consumer-centric perspective. It also focuses on the effects of the adoption of green practices and does not recapitulate the status quo, considering multiple aspects of website design in the context of a sophisticated discrete choice experiment. Finally, it determines which characteristics of green website design actually communicate sustainability best.

title: Factors Influencing Job Satisfaction Among Tourism and Hospitality Undergraduate Students: A Path to a Sustainable Tourism Industry in Bangladesh

detail.abstract: Purpose: The tourism industry in Bangladesh presents a promising avenue for economic expansion and employment generation. Many undergraduate students in Bangladesh work part-time or full-time in this field while studying. This study aims to explore the factors that determine the job satisfaction of these tourism and hospitality undergraduate students, addressing a gap in existing research. Research Methodology: A convenience sample of 118 undergraduate students from five universities was surveyed using a structured questionnaire. The data were analyzed using SPSS 25, and multiple linear regression analysis was employed to assess the impact of various factors on job satisfaction. Results: The findings reveal that compensation and benefits, communication, opportunities for growth, and the nature of the work significantly influence job satisfaction, whereas work environment and company policy have a comparatively weaker association. Limitations: The small sample size and the use of a non-probability sampling method have limited the generalizability of the present study, which may not fully represent the broader student workforce in the tourism sector. Contribution: This research provides actionable insights for industry leaders and HR professionals in the tourism and hospitality sector, helping them to better understand and enhance job satisfaction among student employees. Novelty: This is the first comprehensive study to investigate the determinants of job satisfaction among tourism and hospitality undergraduate students in Bangladesh who are currently engaged in academic studies and employment.

title: Parasocial Relationships and Consumer Trust: The Role of Influencer Endorsements on Instagram
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Parasocial Relationships and Consumer Trust: The Role of Influencer Endorsements on Instagram
detail.abstract: The rise of social media influencers has reshaped modern marketing by creating intimate yet one-sided interactions known as parasocial relationships. This paper examines how such relationships influence consumer trust and purchasing behavior on Instagram. By synthesizing insights from consumer psychology, marketing theory, and digital communication research, the study highlights how influencers serve as trusted intermediaries, blending personal narratives with product endorsements to affect brand perception. The analysis explores the mechanisms through which perceived authenticity, credibility, and emotional connection enhance consumer trust, ultimately driving engagement and purchase intentions. Additionally, the paper considers the ethical implications of influencer marketing, including transparency, disclosure, and consumer vulnerability. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of digital marketing strategies and provide practical insights for businesses aiming to leverage influencer relationships effectively while maintaining consumer trust.

title: Digital Marketing Strategies and Small Business Growth: Evidence from Nigerian Small and Medium Enterprises
affiliations: Lead City University - Department of Management and Accounting

detail.title: Digital Marketing Strategies and Small Business Growth: Evidence from Nigerian Small and Medium Enterprises
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between digital marketing strategies and small business growth in Nigeria, focusing on small and medium enterprises (SMEs) operating in Ibadan, Oyo State. Using a quantitative research design with a cross-sectional survey approach, data was collected from 292 small business owners and managers across various sectors. The study employed linear regression analysis to assess hypotheses regarding the impact of social media marketing on revenue growth and search engine marketing on customer base expansion. Results reveal that social media marketing strategies have a significant positive relationship with revenue growth (R = .724, p < 0.01), accounting for 52.4% of revenue variations. Similarly, search engine marketing demonstrates a significant impact on customer base expansion (R = .658, p < 0.01), explaining 43.3% of customer base variations. These findings provide empirical evidence for the effectiveness of digital marketing strategies in driving business growth among Nigerian SMEs and offer valuable insights for practitioners and policymakers in emerging markets.

title: A Study on the Influence of the Country of Origin on Women's Purchasing Behavior: A Case Study of Kitenge Garment
affiliations: University of Rwanda, Indira Gandhi National Open University, Mercer University-Atlanta, University of Rwanda and University of Rwanda

detail.title: A Study on the Influence of the Country of Origin on Women's Purchasing Behavior: A Case Study of Kitenge Garment
detail.abstract: This study analyzes the impact of the nation of origin on women's purchasing behaviors of Kitenge garments. A discussion with a few women was organized to gain insight into their purchasing behavior for kitenge garments, particularly in the country whose kitenge garment is preferred, and the attributes they seek when planning to buy it. Responses obtained were used to develop an instrument for the study. A sample of 100 Women was selected, considering that women are the major users of Kitenge garments. A descriptive design was employed, utilizing convenience sampling as the sampling technique. A personal interview was used as a data collection technique. The findings showed that 82 percent of respondents were aware of the presence of imported Kitenge garments in the market. Regarding the country of origin whose imported kitenge garment is preferred, respondents ranked the Netherlands first, followed by Senegal, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and the United Kingdom. Concerning the attributes that influence the purchase of Kitenge garments, the texture was ranked first, followed by the country of origin, price, appearance (color), brand name, and durability. The findings would be very useful to the local manufacturers of Kitenge as they will understand what factors influence women to buy Kitenge garments, thereby making their products more competitive. Managerial implications have also been discussed.

title: Product Differentiation through Labels: Evidence from EU Energy Relabeling
affiliations: KU Leuven, KU Leuven - Faculty of Business and Economics (FEB), University of Hamburg, affiliation not provided to SSRN and KU Leuven

detail.title: Product Differentiation through Labels: Evidence from EU Energy Relabeling
detail.abstract: We study how greater product differentiation in energy label classes affects consumer sales decisions. We exploit the 2021 rescaling of the EU Energy Label, which replaced the crowded A-plus ratings (A+, A++, A+++) with a simpler A-G scale and expanded the number of available classes. Using weekly transaction data of refrigerators and freezers from nine European retailers, we find that the rescaling shifted sales toward more energy-efficient models, primarily in the medium-efficiency segment where differentiation changed the most. In this group, the broad A++ class was split roughly evenly into the new E and F classes, leading to a 7 percentage point shift in market shares from F-to E-class models as a result of the rescaling. This shift reduced the average electricity consumption of sold models by 7.5 kWh per year, or 3.5%. Our findings suggest that reducing the coarseness of energy label classes can be an effective way of conveying efficiency information without increasing cognitive burden.

title: Brand Hate Detector: An R Shiny Application for Automated Detection and Multilevel Classification of Brand Hate in Consumer Reviews
affiliations: Hassan First University Of Settat

detail.title: Brand Hate Detector: An R Shiny Application for Automated Detection and Multilevel Classification of Brand Hate in Consumer Reviews
detail.abstract: The Brand Hate Detector is an open-source R Shiny application designed to identify, classify, and visualize brand hate in online consumer reviews. Unlike traditional sentiment analysis tools that reduce feedback to simple positive-negative polarity, the Brand Hate Detector employs a hybrid lexicon-based approach that integrates sentiment polarity, emotion profiling using the NRC Emotion Lexicon, and rule-based classification to capture multiple hate intensity levels. The workflow includes automated scraping of brand-specific reviews from ConsumerAffairs.com, negative sentiment filtering, stopword removal, emotion analysis, and a two-stage classification process that assigns reviews to Mild, Moderate, Strong, or Hybrid hate categories. Results are presented through interactive visualizations, including category distributions, reason-specific breakdowns, emotion word clouds, and sentiment-intensity bubble plots. Designed for transparency, reproducibility, and accessibility, the tool bridges academic theory and managerial practice by providing actionable insights into the drivers and emotional dynamics of consumer hostility toward brands. Its modular architecture also allows future extensions to other review platforms, additional languages, and machine learning-based classification methods.

reference: International Journal of Environmental Sciences, 2025[10.64252/tnb75893]
title: Impact Of Digital Analytics On Brand Engagement Effectiveness

detail.title: Impact Of Digital Analytics On Brand Engagement Effectiveness

publicationDetails.detailsText: International Journal of Environmental Sciences, 2025[10.64252/tnb75893]

detail.abstract: Digital analytics in e-commerce created a new manner in which brands connect with their consumers. The evaluation of digital analytics tools namely AI algorithms and machine learning techniques and IoT applications examines their effect on Amazon India's engagement strategy across the Indore district. The survey research included 120 Amazon user responses from Indore City. Digital analytics tools act as a strong driver which boosts brand engagement through their power to explain 50% of its changing pattern. Consumer purchases and brand engagement outcome results from social media interactions through Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn and YouTube (R² = 0.338 along with R² = 0.539) show that online connections significantly affect buying choices. Consumer loyalty toward brands depends on online verbal endorsements and sudden purchasing reactions according to the research findings. The research findings offer essential guidance to businesses which helps them tweak their digital methods while maximizing customer relations and improving brand customer retention. The research exclusivity to Indore city does not restrict the discoveries from delivering meaning to ecommerce markets on a wider scale. Future investigators should examine matched factors across various regions to establish the complete scope of digital analytics in consumer engagement processes. The research enhances prevailing discussions regarding data-based marketing methods and their capacity to build enhanced brand connections between businesses and consumers during digital times.

title: THE ROLE OF SOCIAL MEDIA IN SHAPING CONSUMER CHOICES AND SOCIAL INTERACTIONS AMONG BANGALORE'S MILLENNIAL POPULATION-A REVIEW
affiliations: REVA Business School (RBS), REVA University

detail.title: THE ROLE OF SOCIAL MEDIA IN SHAPING CONSUMER CHOICES AND SOCIAL INTERACTIONS AMONG BANGALORE'S MILLENNIAL POPULATION-A REVIEW
detail.abstract: The rapid penetration of digital technologies and the rise of interactive platforms have positioned social media as a powerful force influencing consumer decisions and shaping social interactions, particularly among millennials. In Bangalore, a city characterized by its vibrant youth demographic and technological advancement, social media has emerged as a dominant medium guiding purchase intentions, lifestyle choices, and peer-to-peer communication. This review study critically examines existing literature on how social media platforms affect consumer preferences, trust formation, and social dynamics among Bangalore's millennial population. The findings suggest that millennials rely heavily on digital reviews, influencer recommendations, peer feedback, and brand narratives shared across platforms such as Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube when making purchase decisions. Beyond consumption, social media also plays a pivotal role in constructing identity, fostering online communities, and reinforcing social belonging. However, the review highlights certain limitations, including issues of information overload, digital fatigue, and the challenge of distinguishing authentic content from sponsored messages. The study underscores the need for businesses to design culturally relevant, transparent, and interactive digital marketing strategies to effectively engage millennial audiences. Implications extend to policymakers and educators, as social media continues to influence not only consumption patterns but also communication styles and social cohesion. Future research should adopt mixed-method approaches to investigate long-term behavioral changes, generational differences, and the evolving role of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, augmented reality, and virtual influencers in shaping consumer and social behaviors within urban Indian contexts.

reference: EMAC 2025
title: Influencing Social Impressions Through Visually Induced Temperature in a Social Networking Site
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School - Department of Marketing, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Influencing Social Impressions Through Visually Induced Temperature in a Social Networking Site

publicationDetails.detailsText: EMAC 2025

detail.abstract: Online social networking sites, such as LinkedIn, have become integral tools for career management purposes. Extant research has explored a range of explicit cues (e.g., textual descriptions related to education, work experience) individuals use in their impression management efforts. However, the literature has yet to pay attention to the effects of implicit cues in online settings. In the present research, we rely on the theory of grounded cognition to advance the field of consumer behavior by examining how the use of visual cues with metaphorical associations related to concrete experiences (i.e., temperature) may influence the perception of an individual's personality traits related to these concrete experiences (warmth, competence, coolness). We find that a LinkedIn banner image associated with hot temperatures can enhance the perception of warmth-related traits, but only when used by a female, and that an image associated with cold temperatures can enhance competence perceptions, but only when used by a male. Our findings suggest that high levels of concreteness in the concepts that the images evoke are critical for these effects to occur. The present work demonstrates that visual cues related to grounded experiences can enhance social perceptions in digitally mediated career settings. The present work represents a steppingstone for intriguing future research in the information systems literature leveraging the theory of grounded cognition in career-related platforms to influence social perception.

title: Who gets hit first and who recovers last? Evidence from Indian Coastal Flood Shock
affiliations: American University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Who gets hit first and who recovers last? Evidence from Indian Coastal Flood Shock
detail.abstract: Catastrophic floods directly risk 1.8 billion lives worldwide, most of whom are from East and South Asia. How do extreme floods reshape paid labor outcomes? To answer this, I focus on a 1-in-100 year flood event in India. I first combine Sentinel-1 SAR with JRC Global Surface Water dataset to generate flood map. Using information from this map in various rounds of periodic labor force surveys, I estimate gender-specific dynamic effects of the flood shock. Key results show that men experienced short-lived reduction in their employment while women faced a delayed but persistent decline in their working hours. Men suffered most in secondary sector and increased their participation in primary sector. Women were hit hardest in the tertiary sector. Such sectoral impacts could be attributable to disruptions in infrastructure and physical capital. Moreover, marital status and dependency burden further shape the gender differential effects of the extreme flood event.

title: The Effects of Personal Income Taxes on Organization Performance: Evidence from Name, Image, and Likeness Compensation Rules
affiliations: North Carolina State University - Department of Accounting and University of Navarra, IESE Business School

detail.title: The Effects of Personal Income Taxes on Organization Performance: Evidence from Name, Image, and Likeness Compensation Rules
detail.abstract: We examine whether personal income taxes affect organization performance. We use the 2021 introduction of Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) compensation rules in U.S. college sports, which removed the ban for athletes to earn income for their sports performance while maintaining their eligibility, as a natural experiment. Exploiting novel performance data, we find that teams in low-tax rate states have approximately three more wins per season than schools in high-tax states post-NIL. The effects of personal income taxes on wins are more pronounced among elite conference schools and schools that can attract top recruits. We also find that if elite conference schools are located in low-tax-rate states, they are more likely to advance to the final stages of the championship tournament. Finally, we provide evidence for the mechanism behind improved organizational outcomes: We show that top-ranked recruits are significantly more likely to choose schools in low-tax-rate states after the implementation of NIL. Collectively, our findings show that individual taxation is linked to talent mobility and thus to organizational success.

title: High vs. Low AGI: Ontology and Conceptual Taxonomy for Geopolitical Coherence
affiliations: Principal Researcher

detail.title: High vs. Low AGI: Ontology and Conceptual Taxonomy for Geopolitical Coherence
detail.abstract: The rapid progression of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) research demands conceptual tools capable of distinguishing between systems developed for open, commercial integration and those destined for sovereign, securitized deployments. Without such distinctions, risk assessments and regulatory debates collapse AGI into legacy dual-use frameworks that are ill-suited for these resources, capturing the possibility of civilian and military application but overlooking the distinct societal lineages yielded by corporate and state-grade architectures. This paper proposes a taxonomy distinguishing low-AGI and high-AGI, clarifying how commercial-economic and security-sovereign architectures can be distinguished not only by function, but by the social and political ecosystems that produce them. The taxonomy builds on international relations concepts of "high/low politics," viewed through the lens of construal-level theory, which allows it to even capture how cooperation and conflict may coexist in the context of AGI's emerging geopolitical stakes. By embedding AGI within power structures and securitization theory, this contribution extends dual-use discourse through an ontological taxonomy that enables more granular risk assessment and governance design-equipping policymakers and researchers to anticipate security dilemmas, institutional demands, and technical-political spillovers in the international system.

title: International trends in innovative development of FoodTech
affiliations: MGIMO (Moscow State University of International Relations)

detail.title: International trends in innovative development of FoodTech
detail.abstract: The study of current global trends in the innovative development of FoodTech is relevant and significant at the present time, as it allows us to identify key areas of research and development, assess their impact on the commodity and geographical structure of the global food market, and consider the prospects for the development of the industry on a global scale. Among the main conclusions, the uneven development of FoodTech technologies in different regions of the world is noted.

title: How much do artisanal miners earn? An inquiry among Congolese gold miners
affiliations: University of Antwerp - Institute of Development Policy and Management, University of Antwerp - Institute of Development Policy and Management and University of Antwerp - Institute of Development Policy and Management

detail.title: How much do artisanal miners earn? An inquiry among Congolese gold miners

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Permission to conduct the research was granted by the University of Antwerp’s Ethics Committee for the Social Sciences and Humanities (file nr. SHW_15_06), by the Congolese Ministry of Mines, by SAESSCAM (the Congolese public Service for Assistance to Artisanal and Small-Scale mining) and by the local authorities in Kamituga.
