The volatility dynamics revealed in this analysis can be incorporated into their portfolio management.

title: Dear Brothers and Sisters: Pope's Speeches and the Dynamics of Conflict in Africa
affiliations: ENS de Lyon, ENS de Lyon, ENS de Lyon and University of Bologna

detail.title: Dear Brothers and Sisters: Pope's Speeches and the Dynamics of Conflict in Africa
detail.abstract: Public speeches by leaders can serve as a cost-effective tool for fostering peace, yet their effectiveness remains uncertain, particularly in divided societies experiencing violent conflict. This paper examines the impact of the Catholic Pope's peace-promoting speeches on conflict dynamics in Africa. We construct a novel dataset covering all papal speeches explicitly addressing violent conflict events in Africa between 1997 and 2022. Using event-study methods, we find that such speeches reduce overall conflict by 23% on average in the weeks following their delivery. Importantly, the effects vary systematically by papal identity: speeches delivered by John Paul II and Francis are associated with substantial reductions in conflict, whereas those delivered by Benedict XVI show no significant aggregate effect and are instead linked to increases in battles and religious violence. We further explore four mechanisms driving these heterogeneous effects. First, the impact of papal speeches is significantly stronger in areas with a Catholic presence, where violence drops by up to 69%. Second, the effectiveness of a speech depends on the bishops' ideological alignment with the Pope's vision, with speeches delivered by a Pope who appointed the current bishop being 17% more effective. Third, political leaders play a crucial role in amplifying the Pope's message, as violence significantly declines in birth regions of national leaders. Finally, the response of armed groups varies depending on their religious affiliation and prior history of violence.

title: Measuring Coalition Power in a Fragmented Parliament: A Shapley-NOMINATE Analysis of the 2022-2024 French Elections
affiliations: Université Le Havre

detail.title: Measuring Coalition Power in a Fragmented Parliament: A Shapley-NOMINATE Analysis of the 2022-2024 French Elections
detail.abstract: In 2022 and 2024, French parliamentary elections have not yielded a stable winning coalition, successive governments had to rely on ad hoc majorities as a result. We combine the Shapley-Shubik model with fuzzy coalition commitment and a Poole-Rosenthal ranking in order to show that there are unstable coalitions that form among the three main blocs, but: a) ideological distances preclude many potential coalitions, b) the restricted core of feasible winning coalitions inflates the bargaining power of smaller parties and groups and c) Coalescing into a larger caucus does not guarantee a larger Shapley value.

title: Chasing Growth, Breathing Smog: The Environmental Outcomes of Target Progress Shortfalls in China
affiliations: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE), Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE) and Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE)

detail.title: Chasing Growth, Breathing Smog: The Environmental Outcomes of Target Progress Shortfalls in China
detail.abstract: Persistent air pollution in China is widely linked to growth-oriented governance, yet little is known about how interim progress toward economic targets shapes short-term environmental outcomes. This paper examines whether temporary shortfalls within the annual growth target cycle induce local governments to relax environmental enforcement. Applying a regression discontinuity design to the city–quarter panel data, we find that cities narrowly missing quarterly milestones experience a 2.3 percent increase in PM2.5 concentrations in the subsequent quarter. The effect is concentrated in the second through fourth quarters and in the latter two months of each quarter, when the annual growth target exerts stronger incentive effects and information on the previous quarter’s economic performance becomes available. Mechanism analysis shows that local officials strategically reduce enforcement intensity, lowering penalty frequency, tolerating highly polluting production, and shifting from strict sanctions to lenient warnings. The effect is stronger when promotion incentives are salient and weaker when environmental constraints are tight. Our findings extend the literature from target setting to target execution and demonstrate how interim progress pressures generate immediate environmental costs, offering new insight into the dynamics of target-based governance.

title: Learning Illiquid Asset Prices
affiliations: Stanford University - Department of Management Science & Engineering, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Stanford University - Department of Management Science & Engineering

detail.title: Learning Illiquid Asset Prices
detail.abstract: Many asset classes-including private equity, real estate, corporate, municipal, and mortgage bonds, as well as structured products-are illiquid, with prices that are observed only sporadically. Yet frequent, objective, and accurate price estimates are essential for portfolio valuation, investment decision-making, and regulatory compliance. This paper develops point and interval estimators for illiquid asset prices, offering both consistency guarantees and non-asymptotic coverage for the resulting intervals. The estimators are based on a scalable, assumption-light semiparametric conditional factor model for the quantiles of asset prices. Empirical results for mortgage-backed securities demonstrate the method's effectiveness and represent the first treatment of illiquid MBS pricing in the literature, highlighting the bond and market characteristics that drive prices.

title: Climate change and income inequality in Sub-Saharan African countries
affiliations: University of Eldoret, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Northwestern Polytechnical University and Southwest University

detail.title: Climate change and income inequality in Sub-Saharan African countries
detail.abstract: The potential for a feedback relationship between climate change and income inequality has become a concern in sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries due to its significant environmental and socio-economic impacts. This study aims to inform policymakers on ways to address inequality and climate resilience in the region simultaneously. It examines the relationship between climate change and income inequality in SSA countries, focusing on Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda, by analyzing data from these three countries between 2009 and 2023. The Dumitrescu and Hurlin adaptation of the Granger causality test and pooled ordinary least squares research techniques were used in the analysis. The results of the pooled ordinary least squares model reveal that rising income inequality has a positive impact on climate change. Conversely, climate change exhibits a positive impact on income inequality. The Dumitrescu-Hurlin causality evidence indicates a strong, bidirectional relationship between climate change and income inequality in the three countries. This implies that the lagged value of climate change explains the variation in income inequality, with a feedback response where the lagged value of income inequality is instrumental in predicting climate change. The study suggests implementing inclusive economic growth and development policies aligned with climate mitigation measures and adaptation objectives.

title: Central Bank Digital Currencies and Private Tokenized Finance: Coexistence
affiliations: Cracow University of Economics, Anambra State Polytechnic, Mgbakwu, Anambra State Polytechnic, Mgbakwu and Federal College of Agriculture

detail.title: Central Bank Digital Currencies and Private Tokenized Finance: Coexistence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of inrerest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: It requires no ethics-related approval except for where we have an anonymous.
declarations.funderStatement: Its not a funded article

keywords: or Collision? Central bank digital currency

detail.abstract: The rapid proliferation of privately issued tokenized assets and decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols is occurring in parallel with global central bank efforts to design and deploy central bank digital currencies (CBDCs). This dual evolution presents a critical juncture for the future of money: Will public digital currencies coexist with and enhance private tokenized finance, or will structural incompatibilities lead to market fragmentation, regulatory conflict, and systemic instability? This research investigates the economic, technical, and policy dimensions of this emerging tension through a mixed-methods approach combining on-chain data analysis, comparative case studies of CBDC pilots, and expert interviews with central bankers, DeFi developers, and financial regulators. Focusing on interoperability, monetary sovereignty, and financial stability, the study examines three core questions: (1) Under what conditions can CBDCs serve as settlement rails for private tokenized assets without compromising monetary policy autonomy? (2) How do design choices in CBDC architecture-such as programmability, privacy, and access-affect their compatibility with DeFi ecosystems? (3) What governance mechanisms can align public and private digital money to support inclusive, efficient, and resilient financial markets? Drawing on evidence from the digital euro, China's digital yuan, Project Aurum (BIS), and Project mBridge , the research proposes a "layered monetary architecture" in which CBDCs anchor trust and stability while private tokenized assets drive innovation and accessibility. The study contributes the first integrated framework for assessing monetary layer compatibility and offers actionable policy guidance for central banks seeking to harness-rather than resist-the tokenization wave.

title: Effect of excise taxes on economic growth in Southeast Europe
affiliations: University of Eldoret, Southwest University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Northwestern Polytechnical University

detail.title: Effect of excise taxes on economic growth in Southeast Europe
detail.abstract: The rapid increase in government expenditure in European member states has raised concerns among policymakers regarding the role of tax revenue generation and its impact on economic growth. The study aims to determine how excise duty revenue influences economic growth in Southeastern Europe (SEE), considering the dual roles of excise taxes in revenue collection and as regulatory tools. It examines how different excise duty policies relate to economic performance and regional integration. Although existing literature addresses fiscal and regulatory issues of excise duties, less attention has been given to their broader macroeconomic implications, such as effects on economic growth and market cohesion within the diverse policy environment of SEE. The study analyzed the impact of excise taxes on economic growth in Romania, Bulgaria, Greece, and Serbia, using panel data from 2006 to 2023 and employing panel least squares estimation. Results indicate that excise tax revenue, gross capital formation, and trade openness positively influence economic growth, while inflation has a negative effect. The study proposes optimal excise tax rates and structures aligned with broader economic objectives. These should avoid depressing consumption or deterring investment in sectors that promote innovation and human capital development. Carefully calibrated tax rates, policies, and revenue administration efforts can facilitate growth without undermining key industries.

title: SIMPLIFIED GUIDE TO AN EFFECTIVE AML AUDIT UNDER THE BSA
affiliations: DERISKING ADVISORY / Global Association of Certified Anti-illicit Financial Flows (GACAIFFP)/ African Society for Corporate Compliance et Ethics (ASCCE)

detail.title: SIMPLIFIED GUIDE TO AN EFFECTIVE AML AUDIT UNDER THE BSA
detail.abstract:
This simplified guide begins by summarizing the basic principles of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Fundamental section, and ensuring short

Parts address specific requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), the USA PATRIOT Act, and the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This is

followed by practical considerations of achieving an effective AML/CFT compliance program, such as Risk Assessment, Know Your Customer,

Transactions Monitoring and Investigations. Measuring the current scale of money laundering is extremely difficult; the World Bank (WB) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have estimated that the volume of money laundering is between 3 and 5 percent of the global gross domestic product (GDP), equivalent to approximately $ 2,2 trillion to $ 3,7 trillion annually.

title: When Machines Meet Each Other: Network Effects and the Strategic Role of History in Multi-Agent AI Systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Fudan University - School of Management, Fudan University - School of Management and Fudan University

detail.title: When Machines Meet Each Other: Network Effects and the Strategic Role of History in Multi-Agent AI Systems
detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) enters the agentic era, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents that interact with one another rather than operate in isolation. This shift raises a fundamental question: how do machine agents behave in interdependent environments where outcomes depend not only on their own choices but also on the coordinated expectations of peers? To address this question, we study LLM agents in a canonical network-effect game, where economic theory predicts convergence to a fulfilled expectation equilibrium (FEE). We design an experimental framework in which 50 heterogeneous GPT-5-based agents repeatedly interact under systematically varied network-effect strengths, price trajectories, and decision-history lengths. The results reveal that LLM agents systematically diverge from FEE: they underestimate participation at low prices, overestimate at high prices, and sustain persistent dispersion. Crucially, the way history is structured emerges as a design lever. Simple monotonic histories-where past outcomes follow a steady upward or downward trend-help stabilize coordination, whereas non-monotonic histories amplify divergence and path dependence. Regression analyses at the individual level further show that price is the dominant driver of deviation, history moderates this effect, and network e!ects amplify contextual distortions. Together, these findings advance machine behavior research by providing the first systematic evidence on multi-agent AI systems under network e!ects and o!er guidance for configuring such systems in practice.

title: QFII-Invested Mutual Fund Managers: Learning from Domestic Peers
affiliations: University of Reading - ICMA Centre and University of Reading - ICMA Centre

detail.title: QFII-Invested Mutual Fund Managers: Learning from Domestic Peers
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how foreign institutional investors, specifically Qualified Foreign Institutional Investors (QFIIs), influence the investment strategies of Chinese mutual fund management companies (FMCs) in which they hold shares. By analysing panel data from 1,766 mutual funds managed by 44 foreign-invested FMCs in China between 2005 and 2021, we explore whether QFII-invested FMCs (Q-FMCs) learn more from their domestic counterparts (D-FMCs) than other foreign-invested FMCs (NQ-FMCs). Our findings show that Q-FMC-managed mutual funds exhibit portfolio allocations more closely aligned with local DFMCs than those managed by NQ-FMCs. This imitation is particularly pronounced when selecting new stocks, enhancing portfolio performance, but not when rebalancing existing positions. Additionally, Q-FMCs trade more actively than NQ-FMCs. Robustness checks confirm these results across various ownership structures, fund characteristics, market conditions, and regulatory changes. These findings highlight the dual role of QFIIs as both investors and learners in China’s evolving financial landscape, offering insights into how foreign capital integrates into emerging mutual fund markets, informing regulatory policy aimed at fostering cross-border financial development.

title: Economic Policy Uncertainty and Non-Performing Loans in Bangladesh
affiliations: Western Sydney University

detail.title: Economic Policy Uncertainty and Non-Performing Loans in Bangladesh
detail.abstract: Using annual data from 2000 to 2021, this study estimates Newey-West corrected OLS models that include crisis episodes, financial depth, sovereign debt, remittance inflows, and institutional quality. The findings reveal a counterintuitive pattern: higher global economic policy uncertainty (GEPU) is associated with lower reported growth in non-performing loans (NPLs) 1. This negative coefficient indicates a masking mechanism where banks restrict credit supply and regulators delay recognising losses, concealing actual NPLs as risks accumulate unseen. Interaction effects suggest that domestic structures influence this relationship: more developed private credit markets and increasing public debt amplify exposure to shocks, while institutional quality reduces long-term defaults but may encourage short-term moral hazard during crises. Robustness checks using different GEPU measures, lag structures, and remittance interactions confirm the context-dependent nature of these results. The main implication is that declining NPL ratios amid global uncertainty are statistical illusions of stability, hiding underlying fragility. Policy priorities include rules-based loan classification, forward-looking provisioning, sovereign exposure caps, SME liquidity facilities, and governance reforms to transform superficial calm into genuine resilience. 1 The two-lag GEPU coefficients are negative and statistically significant across all three specifications (-0.030 **,-0.168 *,-0.158 *), indicating that a rise in global economic policy uncertainty is associated with a subsequent decline in the growth of reported non-performing loans in Bangladesh. "An economic underground can come to life if firms have an incentive to go broke for profit at society's expense (to loot) instead of to go for broke (to gamble on success)." Akerlof and Romer, 1994

title: Unrefined national building inventories can mislead risk assessments and decisions
affiliations: Dartmouth College - Thayer School of Engineering, Los Alamos National Laboratory, Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Rice University - Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Dartmouth College, Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Cornell University, Government of the United States of America - Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and Dartmouth College - Thayer School of Engineering

detail.title: Unrefined national building inventories can mislead risk assessments and decisions
detail.abstract: Flood-risk assessments inform consequential public decisions. These assessments increasingly use large-scale building inventories that offer granular details but come with little quality assurance. The U.S. Army Corps' National Structure Inventory (NSI) is a prominent example. The Corps explicitly recommends that users evaluate data quality and adjust attributes as necessary. However, many studies skip this step. This raises the questions: How accurate is the NSI and how do any errors influence risk assessments and decisions? Here we use a case study for the city of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania comparing NSI-based damage estimates against estimates with highquality, feature-rich local building data under an ensemble of flood scenarios. The nearly ubiquitous practice of adopting the NSI without refinements can systematically distort flood damage estimates with potentially drastic implications for resource allocation decisions. Using the NSI to rank census tracts by damage-a common metric for prioritizing federal disaster funding-generally misclassifies one-fifth of tracts regarding their priority status. Simple refinements, such as correcting building locations, can drastically reduce classification errors, leading to correct identification of all tracts with respect to priority status in all but one flood scenario. Our findings demonstrate how the use of unrefined nationwide building inventories can compromise risk assessments and mislead resource allocation. We provide actionable guidance for enhancing inventory reliability to improve risk estimation and decision analyses.

title: Financial literacy indicators and poverty
affiliations: Menno Simons College

detail.title: Financial literacy indicators and poverty

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was granted by the CMU research ethics board.

detail.abstract: This report examines the relationship between financial literacy indicators and poverty, questioning assumptions that low-income individuals are inherently less financially literate. 2 It critiques conventional frameworks, often grounded in rational actor models, for emphasizing universal measures such as numeracy and compound interest, which may not align with the realities of poverty. Drawing on critical social science and the Canadian Financial Diaries, it highlights how access to institutions, community supports, and personal capacity shape financial literacy. The study proposes context-sensitive indicators, recognizing that effective financial management among low-income people often depends less on numeracy and more on social and institutional factors.

title: Exchange Rate Dynamics Under Uncertainty: Regime Identification, Multi-Agent Expectations, and Market Diagnostics
affiliations: Chu Hai College of Higher Education

detail.title: Exchange Rate Dynamics Under Uncertainty: Regime Identification, Multi-Agent Expectations, and Market Diagnostics

keywords: Simultaneous spot and forward rate pricing

detail.abstract: This study develops a regime-sensitive framework for exchange rate determination that integrates macroeconomic and financial theory with multi-agent expectations. Unlike traditional models with static regime labels or black-box AI systems, our approach endogenizes regime credibility through dispersion of expectations in forward premiums and spot-rate behavior. We price spot rates via a business cycle CAPM, while forward rates reflect regime sustainability and confidence risk. The model embeds dual expectation channels--investment behavior and regime trust--capturing home bias, strategic portfolio allocation, and volatility diagnostics, including smiles, volatility of volatility, and phase maps. Empirical results across floating, fixed, and managed regimes show strong in-and out-of-sample performances. While floating regimes (e.g., DXY, USDJPY) reveal dispersed expectations and intervention-divergent dynamics, fixed regimes (e.g., USDHKD) show tight volatility bands and high predictability, The framework also offers a novel lens on the impossible trinity, showing how volatility structures reflect the trade-offs between monetary autonomy, capital mobility, and exchange rate stability.

title: Gratitude in fundraising: Do 'thank you in advance' and handwritten thank-you notes impact fundraising success?
affiliations: WZB Berlin Social Science Center, Wissenschaftszentrum Berlin für Sozialforschung (WZB) and German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin)

detail.title: Gratitude in fundraising: Do 'thank you in advance' and handwritten thank-you notes impact fundraising success?
detail.abstract: While almost all charities rely on a set of donor appreciation strategies, their effectiveness for the success of fundraising campaigns is underresearched. Through two preregistered field studies conducted in collaboration with a leading German opera house (N=10,000), we explore the significance of expressing gratitude and examine two different approaches to doing so. Our first study investigates the impact of a "thank you in advance" statement in fundraising letters, a common strategy among fundraisers. In the second study, we explore the effectiveness of handwritten thank-you postcards versus printed postcards, shedding light on the roles of personalization and handwriting in donor appeals. Our findings challenge conventional wisdom, revealing that neither "thank you in advance" nor handwritten thank-you notes significantly affect donor contributions.

title: Economic Diplomatic Strategy, Including Technology and Resilient Supply Chains
affiliations: University of Aberdeen

detail.title: Economic Diplomatic Strategy, Including Technology and Resilient Supply Chains
detail.abstract:
In the wake of the protectionist tendencies of the USA and the rise of China, the new international order is witnessing the growing importance of middle-powers. Japan, India, the Republic of Korea, Australia, Canada, Indonesia, Vietnam, Mexico, Turkey, South Africa, and Brazil are prominent nations that can be seen taking up new initiatives in the international arena or building alliances for mutual benefit. The following paper presents a brief report on Australia's economic diplomatic strategy, with a focus on technology and resilient supply chains. The report is in the form of a SWOT analysis, presenting the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats facing the Australian government. It provides suggestive solutions in the sections of weaknesses and threats.

“Stop worrying about the world ending today. It's already tomorrow in Australia.” (Carl Schulz)

title: INSTRUMENTAL FREEDOMS AND ELECTIONS IN COLOMBIAN DEMOCRACY
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: INSTRUMENTAL FREEDOMS AND ELECTIONS IN COLOMBIAN DEMOCRACY

keywords: Ibagué Social and Human Sciences Observatory
Journal of Research in Social and Economic Sciences

detail.abstract: This article analyzes Title IX of Colombia's 1991 Political Constitution, relating to elections and electoral organization, based on Amartya Sen's theoretical framework on instrumental freedoms and the differentiation between agency and choice. It assesses whether constitutional provisions and electoral institutions effectively expand political freedoms, economic facilities, social opportunities, transparency guarantees, and protective security. The analysis, from an economic, legal, and territorial perspective, shows progress in political rights and transparency, but persists in economic inclusion, social opportunities, and protection against electoral violence. It concludes that Colombian electoral democracy partially complies with Sen's approach.

title: Preference Evolution in the Very Long Run
affiliations: University of Oregon - Department of Economics

detail.title: Preference Evolution in the Very Long Run
detail.abstract: This paper revisits a common modeling assumption in the indirect evolution approach, which analyzes the evolution of preferences in strategic interactions: that such evolution unfolds over a moderate time scale. In reality, the relevant evolutionary horizon may exceed the scope for which static solution concepts or deterministic dynamics are usually applied. To address this, we employ stochastic dynamics to model preference evolution. This shift in time scale leads to fundamentally different selection criteria: in the long run, efficiency becomes necessary for stochastic stability, whereas medium-run stability does not generally require it.

title: Bank lending during the Global Financial Crisis credit crunch: Only what matters, capital or liquidity?
affiliations: Université de Sherbrooke, Université de Sherbrooke and Université Laval

detail.title: Bank lending during the Global Financial Crisis credit crunch: Only what matters, capital or liquidity?
detail.abstract: Following the 2007 Global Financial Crisis (GFC) credit crunch, a large literature points to a major role of bank liquidity but other influential works find support to bank capital in fostering bank lending. To dig further in the drivers of bank lending, we employ a novel empirical approach to study the effects of bank beforehand GFC, i.e., ante-GFC  capital and liquidity on bank lending growth during the GFC. We create a treatment indicator to capture banks that were prone to liquidity risk at the outset of the GFC. We find that both US banks’ capital and liquidity affect their ability to lend during the crisis but the capitalization impact is the most crucial one. Holding liquid assets complements building capital only for small banks under $ 1 billion in assets.  Therefore, in implementing Basel III liquidity requirements, regulators should give precedence to bank capital and ensure that small banks hold sufficient liquid assets.

title: How Achievement Emotions Relate to the Short-Term Stability of Goal-Orientation Profiles in an Introduction to Accounting Course
affiliations: University of Eastern Finland and University of Eastern Finland

detail.title: How Achievement Emotions Relate to the Short-Term Stability of Goal-Orientation Profiles in an Introduction to Accounting Course

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval for the study was obtained from the Business School where the study was conducted. Permission was individually sought from each participating student via the cover page of the research questionnaire. Participation was voluntary, and students were informed that their responses would remain confidential and anonymous. The study complied with institutional ethical standards for research involving human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: Author Hannu Ojala has received funding for conferences travelling from the university of Eastern Finland.

detail.abstract: Achievement emotions and achievement goal orientations jointly shape how students engage with demanding coursework. Nevertheless, very little is known about how these two constructs co-evolve within a single Introduction to Accounting course. Drawing on Control-Value Theory and Achievement Goal Theory and using latent profile analysis, we surveyed 98 first-year business students at the start and end of a six-week course. Latent-profile analysis revealed four recurring goal-orientation configurations: Non-Competitive, Somewhat Competitive, Well-Adjusted, and Success-Seeking, which remained structurally stable throughout the term. Roughly two-thirds of students preserved their initial profile; the remainder moved in roughly equal numbers toward different configurations. Logistic-regression results showed that changes in enjoyment or boredom did not predict shifts. Increases in worry significantly triggered them. Increased worry nearly doubled the odds of shifting into a less adaptive profile, even after controlling for gender and high school GPA. This study enriches the motivation literature by documenting within-course dynamism and positions achievement emotions, particularly worry, as critical drivers for sustaining adaptive motivation in numberintensive business education contexts.

title: Payment-In-Kind (PIK) Debt
affiliations: University of Texas at San Antonio - Department of Finance, University of Wisconsin-Madison and

detail.title: Payment-In-Kind (PIK) Debt

keywords: private credit market JEL codes: G12

detail.abstract: PIK debt allows unpaid interest to be capitalized, which raises concerns about weakened lender monitoring rights. We provide the first comparative analysis of PIK bonds using a comprehensive sample. Compared with similar regular high-yield (RHY) bonds, PIK bonds' yield spreads are 1.8 percentage points higher at issuance. Although PIKs are generally issued by riskier borrowers and have a higher average default rate, they are 14.9 percentage points less likely to default than RHY bonds after controlling for bond and issuer characteristics. Our results suggest that PIK debt is a valuable financing tool for financially constrained firms with high growth potential.

title: Automating Insight Extraction from Oil and Gas Sector Climate Disclosures with AI *
affiliations: Amundi Institute, Amundi Asset Management, Amundi Asset Management, Amundi Technology, Amundi Technology and Amundi Institute

detail.title: Automating Insight Extraction from Oil and Gas Sector Climate Disclosures with AI *
detail.abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting has become a cornerstone of corporate transparency and accountability, especially within high emission sectors such as oil and gas. However, the traditional methods of extracting meaningful insights from ESG data are time-consuming and are in general processed manually. In this study, the authors introduce a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, which automates the extraction and evaluation of information across large volumes of general and sustainable reporting, enabling analysts to efficiently process and synthesize data from multiple years and companies. The authors propose evaluation metrics that mimick human assessment. The methodology's scalability and adaptability make it a promising solution for automating the analysis of corporate ESG disclosures on a large scale, thus providing a robust framework for future research and practical applications in corporate sustainability assessment and climate engagement.

reference: Journal of Empirical Legal Studies, Volume 22, No. 3, pp. 270-297 (2025)
title: THE DISTANCE FACTOR IN REMEDIES
affiliations: Hebrew University - Faculty of Law and Hebrew University Jerusalem

detail.title: THE DISTANCE FACTOR IN REMEDIES

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Empirical Legal Studies, Volume 22, No. 3, pp. 270-297 (2025)

detail.abstract: This article proposes a new classification of legal remedies that cuts across existing classifications. It argues that all remedies involving the transfer of resources are positioned along a continuum from close to remote, which determines their "distance factor". The basic distinction is between remedies provided directly by the injurer to the injured and remedies that are provided through third parties. The article presents the results of two original, preregistered experiments designed to examine the effect of the distance factor on perceptions of, and preferences for, various remedies, from the perspectives of both the injured and injurers. The experiments reveal that even when the remedy is monetary, both injured and injurers prefer the remedy with the smaller distance factor. Specifically, both parties believe that direct compensation leads to better outcomes than payment via a third party with regard to rectifying the harm done, granting satisfaction to the injured, treating the injured and injurer with respect, improving the bilateral relations, and increasing the injurer's sense of responsibility for the harm. These findings are relevant to the various goals that the law wishes to promote, such as corrective justice, economic efficiency, or distributive justice. They vindicate the importance of private law, offer a more attractive justification for it than the one offered by Civil Recourse Theory, and support pluralism in remedial modes.

title: On “An” (安): Inner Peace through Uncertainty, Nature Quotient, and Harmony with Dao
affiliations: Phenikaa University, Phenikaa University and Phenikaa University

detail.title: On “An” (安): Inner Peace through Uncertainty, Nature Quotient, and Harmony with Dao
detail.abstract: Inner peace (An, 安) holds profound significance in Chinese and broader East Asian cultures within the Sinosphere. In Confucianism, peace arises from reducing uncertainty through virtuous hierarchies and the conscientious fulfillment of moral obligations that embody Ren (仁), or human-heartedness. Yet such peace is inherently fragile and unsustainable if human-heartedness deviates from the Dao—the natural order of the universe. In contrast, Zhuangzi’s vision of peace, centered on spontaneity, wu-wei (無為), and the rejection of rigid social norms, offers a pathway to genuine freedom and enlightenment. Employing the Granular Interaction Thinking Theory (GITT), this study provides a scientific elaboration of Zhuangzi’s philosophy of inner peace, as expressed in Free and Easy Wandering (Xiao Yao You, 逍遙遊), and examines how such a state may be achieved through cultivating Nature Quotient (NQ). Ultimately, we propose that Daoist philosophy—especially Zhuangzi’s—can underpin a modern paradigm of inner peace that nurtures harmony within individuals, societies, nations, and the global community.

title: INSTRUMENTAL FREEDOMS AND PUBLIC TREASURY IN COLOMBIA
affiliations: EDUKIVOTOS

detail.title: INSTRUMENTAL FREEDOMS AND PUBLIC TREASURY IN COLOMBIA
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the relationship between Amartya Sen's theoretical postulates on instrumental freedoms and the constitutional framework of the Colombian economic regime and public finances, established in Title XII of the 1991 Constitution. It examines the extent to which the five instrumental freedoms-political, economic, social, transparency, and protective security-are reflected in the fiscal, budgetary, and economic organization of the State. The study argues that the tax system partially promotes human agency but is limited by inequality, institutional inefficiency, and limited territorial autonomy. It concludes that the Colombian economic regime requires profound reforms to harmonize public finances with human development and territorial justice.

title: Equilibrium Power Purchase Agreements Through Nash Bargaining Solutions
affiliations: and Amazon

detail.title: Equilibrium Power Purchase Agreements Through Nash Bargaining Solutions
detail.abstract: As electricity demand from hyperscale data centers grows rapidly, many data center operators are turning to long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) to secure low-cost, low-carbon electricity while managing exposure to wholesale market volatility. These contracts are often structured as financial hedges and negotiated directly with renewable power suppliers. In this paper, we model the PPA negotiation process between a data center and a power supplier using a Nash bargaining framework. The equilibrium contract structure-mainly defined by strike price and contract volume-is the solution to a stochastic program that maximizes the product of utility differentials between the two parties, with and without the contract. To capture each party's risk preferences, we employ conditional cash flow at risk (CCFaR), a tail-based profitability measure that quantifies exposure to low-cash-flow outcomes. We incorporate CCFaR into the utility functions and solve the resulting non-convex stochastic program using the Sample Average Approximation (SAA) method. Numerical experiments and sensitivity analyses reveal how equilibrium contract terms are influenced by volatility in spot prices, correlation between price and generation, and differences in the parties' risk aversion. Our results provide a quantitative foundation for understanding how long-term clean energy contracts can be negotiated under asymmetric risk preferences and market uncertainty.

title: Climate Risk and Strategic Green M&As
affiliations: Deakin Business School, Deakin University, Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University) - School of Economics, Finance and Marketing, Deakin University - Deakin Business School and Deakin University

detail.title: Climate Risk and Strategic Green M&As

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no potential conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors declare that they have not received any financial support for the research paper.

detail.abstract: We examine how firms adapt to climate risk through the market for corporate control. Using firm-level measures of climate exposure, we find that more exposed firms are significantly more likely to acquire targets with green technologies and operations. This effect is strongest among firms with limited internal innovation capacity and in industries where offshoring emissions is less feasible. Evidence suggests these acquisitions are value-driven rather than agency-driven, as the effect is concentrated among firms with stronger managerialshareholder alignment, greater analyst coverage, and closer monitoring by socially responsible institutions. Consistent with investor influence, higher climate exposure is associated with increases in socially responsible ownership, the number of climate-related shareholder proposals, and support for such proposals. Green acquisitions also yield positive announcement returns and boost subsequent green innovation, indicating benefits beyond technology transfer. Overall, our results highlight M&A as a strategic, market-based mechanism for corporate adaptation to climate risk.

title: Investor Memory and Stock Returns: Empirical Evidence
affiliations: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE) - China Center for Behavior Economics and Finance and Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE) - China Center for Behavior Economics and Finance

detail.title: Investor Memory and Stock Returns: Empirical Evidence
detail.abstract: We measure investor memory bias (MB) as the proportion of negative daily returns that investors tend to forget or suppress. We find that stocks with high MB earn significantly lower subsequent returns than stocks with low MB. The high-minus-low MB portfolio generates a return spread of-0.90% per month for equal-weighted portfolios and-0.81% per month for value-weighted portfolios. The negative relation between MB and future returns remains after controlling for fifteen established stock characteristics and stays statistically significant under multiple asset-pricing factor models. Further analysis reveals that the MB effect is stronger when investor sentiment is high, when investors use closing prices rather than opening prices, and when arbitrage constraints are tighter. High-MB stocks also exhibit significantly greater abnormal trading volume, consistent with memory-induced reinvestment behavior. Our findings provide the first direct empirical evidence that positive memory bias systematically affects aggregate stock prices.

title: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF MULTIPLE STOCK SCREENING TECHNIQUES ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LISTED MANUFACTURING FIRMS IN BANGLADESH
affiliations: American International University Bangladesh (AIUB)

detail.title: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF MULTIPLE STOCK SCREENING TECHNIQUES ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LISTED MANUFACTURING FIRMS IN BANGLADESH
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the efficacy of various stock screening methods in analyzing the financial distress and performance of listed manufacturing companies in Bangladesh. As financial decision-making becomes increasingly complex, businesses, investors, and policymakers require sound evaluation methodologies to assess the viability and potential growth of firms. This study systematically analyzes several screening techniques (e.g., financial ratios, market, and operational indicators) to evaluate their ability to predict the viability of manufacturing firms. The analysis is conducted on a sample of listed manufacturing companies across various sectors, using a quantitative approach to measure associations between screening variables and performance indicators such as profitability, liquidity, and growth potential. The results indicate that multimethod function testing can create an integrated performance assessment method, providing a richer picture for the decision-making process. This paper contributes to corporate finance literature by demonstrating that a variety of screening tools can be effective for monitoring the manufacturing industry and offers both academic and practical relevance for financial analysts, investors, and firms seeking long-term sustainability.

reference: Finance Research Letters, volume 49, 2022[10.1016/j.frl.2022.103143]
title: Aggregate Investor Attention and Bitcoin Return: The Long Short-term Memory Networks Perspective
affiliations: Tianjin University, School of Finance, Nankai University and University of Hull

detail.title: Aggregate Investor Attention and Bitcoin Return: The Long Short-term Memory Networks Perspective

publicationDetails.detailsText: Finance Research Letters, volume 49, 2022[10.1016/j.frl.2022.103143]

detail.abstract: Investor attention is a scarce cognitive resource which affects investment decisions, and recent studies suggest that investor attention also have impacts on asset prices. Although Bitcoin is found to be one of the most unpredictable cryptocurrencies with excessive volatilities, researchers are still looking for determinants of Bitcoin prices. In this study, we firstly adopt the Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM) approach to evaluate the effect of investor attention on Bitcoin returns by constructing an aggregate investor attention proxy. We combine both direct and indirect proxies for investor attention, in addition to the Bitcoin trading variables as the LSTM inputs. Our empirical results suggest that the including of attention variables could effectively improve the LSTM's prediction accuracy of Bitcoin prices, whereas direct proxies (i.e. daily Google Trends to Bitcoin and Bitcoin tweets) contains more valuable information to further improve the LSTM's forecasting capacity.

reference: Russian Linguistics, volume 49, issue 1, 2025[10.1007/s11185-025-09321-x]
title: A quantitative approach to practical transcription of Japanese names into Ukrainian
affiliations: Institute of Artificial Intelligence Problems

detail.title: A quantitative approach to practical transcription of Japanese names into Ukrainian

publicationDetails.detailsText: Russian Linguistics, volume 49, issue 1, 2025[10.1007/s11185-025-09321-x]

detail.abstract: This study introduces a quantitative phonetic distance metric to evaluate and improve the practical transcription of Japanese names into Ukrainian. We argue for a standardization of Japanese-Ukrainian transcription grounded in objective phonetic similarity, while also proposing a phoneticphonemic model that accounts for coarticulation effects in Japanese. By applying a metric method grounded in articulatory phonetics, this work identifies the clos est phoneme pairs between Japanese and Ukrainian and assesses their alignment in several established transcription systems. Special attention is given to Japanese palatalized conso nants such as [ɕ], [ʑ], and [t͡ ɕ], which correspond more accurately to Ukrainian soft alveolar phonemes [sʲ], [zʲ], and [t͡ sʲ] than to their postalveolar counterparts. The results reveal that the modified Fedoryshyn system-replacing the Ukrainian letter "ґ" ("g") with "г" ("gh")-most closely aligns with both phonetic and phonological principles of the Ukrainian lan guage. Statistical frequency data from the Ukrainian language corpus further support these findings. The metric method used here provides a replicable framework that can be extended to other language pairs and transcription contexts. This approach enhances linguistic preci sion and supports the development of consistent, phonetically accurate, and computationally useful transcription systems.

title: Regulating Cryptocurrency Transactions: International Tax Frameworks, IFRS Convergence, and Cross-Border Arbitrage
affiliations: The University of Lahore Islamabad Campus

detail.title: Regulating Cryptocurrency Transactions: International Tax Frameworks, IFRS Convergence, and Cross-Border Arbitrage
detail.abstract: This study looks at how international tax rules work to control cryptocurrency transactions. It is based on IFRS rules and the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). The researcher uses a new global dataset covering the years 2011 to 2025. The study introduces ten measures: the Global Regulatory Coverage Index (GRCI), the Global IFRS Alignment Score (GIFRSAS), the Global Tax Compliance Effectiveness Score (GTCES), the Global Cross-Border Arbitrage Index (GCBAI), the Global Disclosure Quality Index (GDQI), the Global Enforcement Capacity Score (GECS), the Global Detection Rate (GDR), the Global Penalty Collection Ratio (GPCR), the Global Convergence Score (GCS), and the Global Policy Diffusion Speed (GPDS). These measures show both how much regulation is in place and how well people follow the rules. The study uses several methods, including describing data, looking at how variables are connected, and using time-based analysis to understand how these factors relate to each other. The results show a strong link between how much regulation is in place and cross-border arbitrage, with a correlation of-0.97. This means that when more countries follow CARF and IFRS reporting, there is less chance of people taking advantage of tax differences in different countries. The study shows that working together internationally, spreading new rules quickly, and having strong enforcement are all important for tax compliance and reducing arbitrage. The study adds value by offering an easy-to-use framework, new measures, and important evidence for policymakers. It concludes that international tax changes can help with compliance and reduce arbitrage only when regulation, IFRS alignment, and enforcement all improve at the same time.

title: Corporate Social Irresponsibility: After ESG, activist investors should side with taxpayers
affiliations: Competitive Enterprise Institute and Center for Economic Accountability

detail.title: Corporate Social Irresponsibility: After ESG, activist investors should side with taxpayers
detail.abstract: State and municipal governments across America are engaged in a massive transfer of public resources to private corporate interests in the name of economic development. However, the evidence is clear that these corporate subsidy programs operate more for the benefit of the cronies who control them than for any measurable public interest. At the same time, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing has become increasingly toxic with policymakers, the corporate world, and the voting public. Rather than doubling down on the divisive and increasingly discredited approach of current ESG practice, firms should pivot to an emphasis on first doing no harm economically and protecting the welfare of American taxpayers.

title: Peer Effects and Worker Visibility in Team Production: Evidence from NBA Rookies
affiliations: Yale University - Department of Economics, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Cambridge, Cambridge Judge Business School and Drexel University

detail.title: Peer Effects and Worker Visibility in Team Production: Evidence from NBA Rookies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no conflict of interest to declare.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how peer quality impacts early-career visibility, productivity, and longterm earnings in team-based settings. While high-ability peers can generate positive spillovers, they may limit opportunities for less-experienced individuals to showcase their skills, limiting visibility and career progression. Using National Basketball Association (NBA) data, where rookies are quasi-randomly assigned to teams, we find that stronger teams provide less playing time, especially for lower-ranked picks or those competing with star players in the same position. This reduces experience, performance, and future earnings. A theoretical model identifies reduced exposure as the key mechanism, with broader implications for team-based industries where early exposure shapes career paths.

title: Aggregation Fallacy: An Explanation for Systematic Forecast Bias
affiliations: Emory University - Goizueta Business School, Lehigh University - College of Business and University of Fribourg - Department of Business Administration

detail.title: Aggregation Fallacy: An Explanation for Systematic Forecast Bias
detail.abstract: In forecasting and capital budgeting, managers tend to underestimate costs. Prior research typically attributes this forecast bias to misaligned incentives or imperfect information. We introduce a novel explanation: aggregation fallacy. The key idea is that individuals provide forecasts of aggregate outcomes (e.g., total costs) by erroneously adding component forecasts (e.g., costs in divisions A and B). While such linear aggregation is appropriate for deterministic information (i.e., costs that have been incurred), it can result in systematic bias with probabilistic information (i.e., future costs) due to right skew in cost distributions. In support of our hypotheses, results of several experiments show that aggregation fallacy leads to systematic underestimation of costs. Additional analyses demonstrate that aggregation fallacy is not eliminated by learning and also holds with financial incentives for forecast accuracy. Overall, our study demonstrates that, even with aligned incentives and perfect information, systematic cost underestimation may arise due to aggregation fallacy.

title: Oligopolistic Information Markets
affiliations: University of York and Humboldt University of Berlin - School of Business and Economics

detail.title: Oligopolistic Information Markets
detail.abstract: We develop a model of oligopolistic price competition in information markets where buyers purchase and combine signals from multiple sellers. This nonexclusivity transforms competition into "portfolio competition", with sellers competing against all possible coalitions rather than individual competitors. We fully characterize its pure-strategy competition equilibria and study endogenous entry. In every equilibrium, buyers purchase efficiently from all active sellers. Whether competition protects buyers from rent extraction depends on information complementarities: in duopoly, full extraction occurs if and only if signals are complements; in oligopoly this if-and-only-if condition generalizes to a coalitional "balancedness" condition. With symmetric sellers, balancedness reduces to a geometric test. Entry can paradoxically reduce competitive pressure when entrants provide strong complementarities. Entry is never excessive, contrasting standard oligopoly models where excess results from business-stealing externalities. Instead, efficient entry is always an equilibrium, though insufficient entry equilibria may exist, prompting regulatory intervention.

title: Complementary Learning Approach for Text Classification using Large Language Models
affiliations: Fordham University - Gabelli School of Business

detail.title: Complementary Learning Approach for Text Classification using Large Language Models

keywords: mechanism-based theorizing RUNNING HEAD: Complementary Learning Approach Complementary Learning Approach for Text Classification using Large Language Models large language models

detail.abstract: In this study, we propose a structured methodology that utilizes large language models (LLMs) in a cost-efficient, parsimonious manner that integrates the strengths of scholars and machines while offsetting their respective weaknesses. Our methodology-facilitated through "chain of thought" and "few-shot learning" prompting from computer science-extends best practices for co-author teams in qualitative research to human-machine teams in quantitative research. This allows humans to utilize abductive reasoning and natural language to interrogate not just what the machine has done but also what the human has done. Our method highlights how scholars can manage LLMs' inherent weaknesses using careful, low-cost techniques. We demonstrate how to use the methodology to interrogate human-machine rating discrepancies for a sample of 1,934 press releases announcing pharmaceutical alliances (1990-2017). Managerial Summary Facilitated through "chain of thought" and "few-shot learning" prompting from computer science, we introduce a method of utilizing large language models (LLMs) to efficiently tackle large text corpora that require subject matter expertise to classify properly. The approach combines the contextual understanding, creativity, and ethical judgment of humans with the computational efficiency, rule-derived consistency, and large dataset processing capacity of LLMs. We draw upon and extend best practices for co-author teams in qualitative research to human-machine teams in quantitative research, allowing humans to utilize natural language to interrogate not just what the machine has done but also what the human has done. We demonstrate how to use the methodology on a sample of 1,934 press releases announcing pharmaceutical alliances (1990-2017).

title: The Economics of Working Environments: Evidence from Linked Survey and Register Data
affiliations: Bocconi University - Department of Management and Technology, Copenhagen Business School - Department of Economics, INSEAD - Economics and Political Sciences and

detail.title: The Economics of Working Environments: Evidence from Linked Survey and Register Data
detail.abstract: We use a large-scale survey from Denmark to construct firm-level measures of the working environment capturing its physical, psychological, and social elements. First, to validate our measures, we show that firms with better working environments fare better in unannounced workplace inspections conducted by a government agency. Second, using register data, we show that firms with better working environments have longer employee tenures, and their employees are less likely to be hospitalized or to experience work-related accidents. Finally, firms with better working environments have higher labor productivity and, ultimately, better profitability. Collectively, our findings suggest that improving firms' working environments can be beneficial to both employees and shareholders.

title: On Finding the Optimal Rotation of Principal Components for Structural Interpretation
affiliations: Swiss Finance Institute

detail.title: On Finding the Optimal Rotation of Principal Components for Structural Interpretation
detail.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of interpreting statistical factors derived from principal component analysis (PCA), a common issue in empirical macroeconomics. Traditional methods for rotating these factors to achieve economic meaning are often ad-hoc and subjective. The paper proposes a novel approach that systematically finds an interpretable rotation by maximizing the cosine similarity between the statistical factor loadings and a target structure. The maximization problem is shown to be equivalent to the Orthogonal Procrustes Problem, which has a unique, optimal solution provided by Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). The paper showcases the method by extracting the monetary policy surprise factors proposed by Kroencke et al. (2021).

title: Cybersecurity Threats, Credit Risk, and the Role of Dual Ownership
affiliations: Texas A&M University

detail.title: Cybersecurity Threats, Credit Risk, and the Role of Dual Ownership
detail.abstract: I study how corporate bond markets price cybersecurity risk. Ex-post, bond prices decline significantly following cyberattacks-especially for junk bonds. Ex-ante, a onestandard deviation increase in cyber risk exposure is associated with a 4.3 basis point rise in bond yield spreads. Firms with higher cyber risk also issue bonds with more issuer restrictive covenants. Ownership structure matters: dual ownership-when the same institution holds both debt and equity-attenuates the risk premium to cyberexposed firms. Using mergers among financial institutions as quasi-exogenous shocks to dual ownership, I find that dual holders reduce firm-level cyber risk and mitigate its pricing in the corporate bond market, but interestingly, not in the equity market. These findings have implications for cybersecurity governance, credit contracting, and SEC disclosure rules, highlighting how financial markets internalize operational risks even in the absence of formal regulation.

reference: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money, volume 89, 2023[10.1016/j.intfin.2023.101877]
title: CSR Performance and Firm Idiosyncratic Risk in a Data-Rich Environment: The Role of Retail Investor Attention
affiliations: Capital University of Economics and Business, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics - School of Public Economics & Administration, Capital University of Economics and Business and University of Hull

detail.title: CSR Performance and Firm Idiosyncratic Risk in a Data-Rich Environment: The Role of Retail Investor Attention

keywords: Chinese financial market JEL code: M14

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money, volume 89, 2023[10.1016/j.intfin.2023.101877]

detail.abstract: In the Chinese stock market, there are many retail investors who focus on short-term profits and may consider corporate social responsibility (CSR) differently from institutional investors. We find that CSR significantly reduces firms' idiosyncratic risk in the Chinese financial market. This result still holds after a series of robustness checks with potential endogeneity concerns. We further test the role of CSR as a nonfinancial informational supplement, the interplay of CSR with stock analyst forecasts and the effect of heterogeneity in corporate governance characteristics. Finally, we find that retail investors' attention mediates the relationship between CSR and firms' idiosyncratic risk. Our results have general implications for understanding the impact of CSR on retail investors.

title: Sand in the Wheels: Addressing Runs through Contingent Fees
affiliations: , SKEMA Business School - Université Côte d'Azur and University of Amsterdam - Finance Group

detail.title: Sand in the Wheels: Addressing Runs through Contingent Fees

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The opinions expressed in this paper do not necessarily reflect those of De Nederlandsche Bank.

detail.abstract: We show how escalation of outflows on viable banks can be tempered by automatic stabilizers. The frequency of inefficient runs is reduced by contingent redemption fees. Fee revenues may be retained or used to pay out more withdrawals. When reassigned back to the queue, they reduce strategic uncertainty and improve liquidity allocation, so a high fee is optimal. A 'fee to the unpaid' allocation reduces liquidity provision but reduces run incentives further, allowing lower fees. When liquidity needs are high, the 'fee to the queue' is preferred, whereas when the costs of inefficient runs are high or to limit spillover effects, the 'fee to the unpaid' mechanism proves more effective.

title: Traffic jams and driver behavior archetypes
affiliations: William Howard Taft University

detail.title: Traffic jams and driver behavior archetypes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest in the creation of this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: As no human participants were employed (computer simulation), no ethics approval was necessary.
declarations.funderStatement: The author self-funded the research for this paper.

detail.abstract: Traffic congestion represents a complex urban phenomenon that has been the subject of extensive research employing various modeling techniques grounded in the principles of physics and molecular theory. Although factors such as road design, accidents, weather conditions, and construction activities contribute to traffic congestion, driver behavior and decision-making are primary determinants of traffic flow efficiency. This study introduces a driver behavior archetype model that quantifies the relationship between individual driver behavior and system-level traffic outcomes through game-theoretic modeling and simulation (N = 500,000) of a three-lane roadway. Mann-Whitney U tests revealed statistically significant differences across all utility measures (p < .001, d > 2.0). In homogeneous populations, responsible drivers achieved substantially higher expected utility (M =-0.090) than irresponsible drivers (M =-1.470). However, in mixed environments (50/50), irresponsible drivers paradoxically outperformed responsible drivers (M = 0.128 vs. M =-0.127), illustrating a social dilemma wherein defection exploits cooperation. Pairwise comparisons across the six driver archetypes indicated that all irresponsible types achieved equivalent utilities while consistently surpassing responsible drivers. Lane-specific analyses revealed differential capacity patterns, with lane 1 exhibiting a more pronounced cumulative utility decline. These findings offer a robust framework for traffic management interventions, congestion prediction, and policy design that aligns individual incentives with collective efficiency. Directions for future research were also proposed.

title: Experience-Based Pairwise Comparison Dynamics
affiliations: University of Oregon - Department of Economics

detail.title: Experience-Based Pairwise Comparison Dynamics
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the experience-based payoff comparison dynamics-a deterministic evolutionary process in which each agent, upon having the opportunity to revise her strategy, compares her realized payoff with that of another agent. In a uniformly random pairwise matching environment, this dynamic is markedly more sensitive to the cardinality of the underlying game's payoff structure than standard dynamics based on comparing the expected payoffs of different strategies. This heightened sensitivity yields equilibrium selection results in coordination games without the long waiting times typical of stochastic stability models. We further show that the strictly dominated strategy in the prisoner's dilemma can survive.

title: Backcasting: A Design Thinking Approach to Creating Transformative Futures.
affiliations: Mohammed Bin Rashid School of Government and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Backcasting: A Design Thinking Approach to Creating Transformative Futures.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract:
Backcasting is the process of shaping events to a preferred future. It has five stages: future horizon, present

horizon, push and pull factors, anchor policies, and impact & early warning signals. It uses four iterative processes: imagination, scoping, boundary setting, and assessment, shifting frames from narrow to wide. Backcasting shapes the path toward a preferred future. In a continuous process, listing assumptions and

reflecting on impact (using them as early warning flags) allows backcasters to track future trajectories. It is not a simple exercise; it challenges the policymakers to confront their preconceived notions and hubris. This confrontation is critical as the future is not set in stone and also because the impacts of policy

performance often is a perception of public value delivered.

title: Optimal Privacy Protection in Central Bank Digital Currency
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of International Trade and Economics, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Industrial Bank Co. and Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of International Trade and Economics

detail.title: Optimal Privacy Protection in Central Bank Digital Currency

declarations.funderStatement: Yang acknowledges the financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 72403265), the 75th batch of the General Program of CPSF (Grant No. 2024M753813), and the financial support from the National Social Science Fund of China (Grant No. 24\&ZD053).

detail.abstract: This paper develops a model that incorporates cash, existing digital payments, and central bank digital currency (CBDC), explicitly capturing their differences and interactions. Within this framework, we examine consumers’ payment choices under heterogeneous privacy preferences and analyze the optimal design of CBDC privacy protection. Because consumer privacy must be balanced against the commercial value of payment data, social welfare exhibits an inverted-U relationship with the level of CBDC privacy protection. The cost of using cash, the convenience of existing digital payments, and the fixed per-transaction benefit to digital payment firms increase the optimal level of CBDC privacy protection, whereas the effect of CBDC convenience on this level is ambiguous. The number of CBDC users increases with the cost of using cash and with CBDC convenience but decreases with the convenience of existing digital payments, while whether this number increases with the fixed per-transaction benefit or not is indeterminate. Furthermore, CBDC adoption lowers the user base and profits of existing digital payment firms, yet raises social welfare because it better accommodates heterogeneous privacy preferences.

title: Heterogeneous Predictability on Mutual Fund Alphas: A Sparse Clustering GMM Approach
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong, City University of Hong Kong (CityU) and City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Economics & Finance

detail.title: Heterogeneous Predictability on Mutual Fund Alphas: A Sparse Clustering GMM Approach
detail.abstract: Mutual fund managers' skills, measured by risk-adjusted alphas, are predictable using fund characteristics identified via machine learning (e.g., Kaniel et al., 2023, JFE; DeMiguel et al., 2023, JFE). However, alpha's predictive power varies across funds and periods, with most funds exhibiting negligible alphas. To model the heterogeneous predictability, this paper introduces Sparse Clustering GMM (SCGMM), a nonparametric approach to uncover latent fund group structures. SCGMM clusters funds using estimated alphas and identifies group-specific parameters tied to market predictors. The method accounts for heterogeneity in cross-sectional grouping and time variation mechanisms across predictors, without requiring prior cluster information or time variation specifications. Our proposed estimator is theoretically grounded, ensuring consistency in grouping and estimation of time-varying parameters. Empirical analysis of U.S. data shows that only a small group of mutual funds exhibit alphas predictably driven by market predictors.

title: Household Wealth and Gray Divorce in the United States

detail.title: Household Wealth and Gray Divorce in the United States
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how changes in household wealth affect the likelihood of divorce among older adults aged 50 and above in the United States. Using panel data from the Health and Retirement Study from 1992 to 2018, I first establish a descriptive non-linear relationship between wealth, and divorce probabilities. The likelihood is higher for lower levels of wealth and monotonically declines, but only upto the median-beyond that it remains fairly flat. Extreme changes in wealth, both positive and negative, are associated with higher probability of divorce, as compared to moderate changes. To estimate the causal effects, I use two separate plausibly exogenous shocks to wealth, one from the stock market and the other from the housing market. A $10,000 predicted increase in real wealth driven by the S&P 500 contemporaneously raises divorce chances by 262%, marginally significant with a p-value of 0.06. A similar sized lagged housing market driven wealth increase also boosts divorce likelihood by 300%, significant at 1%. I find little evidence of a non-monotonic effect of these wealth shocks on divorce. These findings contribute to research on late-life divorce determinants and expand analysis of how wealth shocks shape well-being over the life cycle. The results have implications for policies targeting asset fluctuations among older households.

title: Why Bankruptcy Will Keep Eating Mass Torts
affiliations: City University of New York (CUNY) - Department of Law

detail.title: Why Bankruptcy Will Keep Eating Mass Torts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: An entity affiliated with the author's immediate family filed a proof of claim in Rite Aid's bankruptcy, and the author assisted in these efforts.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
Mass tort cases have increasingly migrated to bankruptcy, grabbing headlines and generating controversy. Yet criticism from scholars, courts, and the public could suggest this exodus may be inappropriate and short-lived. This Article argues that this pessimism is misplaced. Instead, bankruptcy’s attraction will survive the Supreme Court’s recent elimination of nonconsensual releases that offer immunity for nondebtors, or limits on divisional mergers that separate assets from liabilities prior to a bankruptcy filing. Tortfeasors value bankruptcy’s jurisdictional reach, negotiating leverage, and permissive institutional environment, and will innovate to sidestep these new constraints. Paraphrasing venture capitalist Marc Andreessen’s view that software will supplant entire industries and thus “eat[] the world,” bankruptcy will keep eating mass torts.

Several underexamined cases illustrate how companies can adapt bankruptcy to allocate liabilities, cap payments, and coerce releases from creditors. In Johnson & Johnson’s third bankruptcy, a divide-and-conquer strategy facilitated near-global settlements and releases for itself and its customers. In Rite Aid’s bankruptcy, secured debt (rather than a divisional merger) cut assets from the grasp of opioid victims, enabling cheap settlements and broad releases. Finally, in Tehum’s bankruptcy, insiders separated assets from liabilities and used other troubling maneuvers to obtain releases while shortchanging tort victims. These show that without nonconsensual releases, debtors will coerce “consent,” while a ban on divisional mergers will not stop them from removing assets from creditors.

Despite the troubling aspects of these cases, this Article argues that mass tort bankruptcies can still be beneficial because they can preserve going-concern value, increase recoveries for individuals, and avoid the uneven recoveries of the tort system. Many of the problems they pose exist regardless of whether nonconsensual nondebtor releases or divisional mergers are permitted. Targeted reforms or better enforcement of existing law can address the most egregious aspects of these cases. And such reforms are needed because bankruptcy will continue to eat mass torts.

title: GLAM-E Lab Response to IPO, DSIT and DCMS Copyright & AI Consultation, February 2025

detail.title: GLAM-E Lab Response to IPO, DSIT and DCMS Copyright & AI Consultation, February 2025
detail.abstract: Much is at stake for the UK’s creative industries and cultural heritage sector, including significant gains. Indeed, there are vast amounts of out-of-copyright materials housed within cultural institutions which can be digitised for text and data mining, new research, creativity and economic growth. We see a crucial opportunity to encourage research and innovation, support the digital transformation of the cultural sector, protect the livelihoods of living creators and our vibrant creative industries, and produce high-quality data for AI development. Our response focuses on the potential of these public domain materials for the development of world-leading AI models and new creative frontiers.

title: National Security Agencies and National Security in Nigeria
affiliations: University of Calabar, Calabar, Nigeria, University of Calabar (UNICAL), University of Calabar and University of Calabar (UNICAL)

detail.title: National Security Agencies and National Security in Nigeria
detail.abstract: One of the top concerns of nations is national security The Nigerian nation is facing several security issues, from farmer-herder clashes to terrorism, armed banditry, among others. Numerous national security agencies, including the Nigerian Army, Navy, Air Force, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS), and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), work together to create a well-coordinated and effective security architecture in response to these complex threats. The function, organisation, coordination, and efficacy of Nigeria's national security services in preserving national security are all examined in this article. Based on theoretical frameworks including the Human Security Paradigm, Systems Theory, and the Realist Theory of State Security, the paper examines how the success of national security plans is influenced by the interplay of institutional capabilities, political will, interagency cooperation, intelligence collection, and community participation. The paper also examines the effects, on the security sector, of interagency rivalry, corruption, poor governance, and outside influences. In order to achieve a safe Nigeria, the necessity of inclusive governance, intelligence-led policing, and security sector reform (SSR) is also emphasized. Within the larger framework of national growth and democratic consolidation, the study adds to the conversation about sustainable security in Nigeria.

reference: Asian Economic Policy Review, 0[10.1111/aepr.70005]
title: Beyond Green: Impacts of Green Bond Issuance on Conventional Bonds in China
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - Chinese Academy of Finance and Development, Fudan University - School of Management, School of Management, Fudan University, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance and University of Macau - Faculty of Business Administration

detail.title: Beyond Green: Impacts of Green Bond Issuance on Conventional Bonds in China

declarations.funderStatement: This work is supported by the Research Grant Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under Grant No. GRF 14501720, 14500621, 15500023, 15500224; the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant No. 72271061 and 2022HWYQ15. Cao acknowledges the support of the PolyU Research Centre for Quantitative Finance (Project P0050344).
