detail.abstract: Food waste contributes approximately 8% of global methane emissions and diverting it from landfills yields significant environmental benefits [1]. As the importance of food waste diversion is becoming recognized globally, a variety of policy initiatives are being implemented to promote diversion [2]. Due to the substantial fraction of waste produced at the household in developed countries, a focus on household diversion is necessary to meet proposed diversion goals [3, 4]. This study examines the impact of residential curbside organics diversion programs, which redirect food waste from high-emission sources (e.g. landfills) to lower-emission sources (e.g. composting), on household food purchases. We use UPC-level food purchasing data for 58,242 households, across 294 cities in the US, from 2004 to 2020 to investigate the effects of composting programs on household food purchases across a five different (potentially) compostable food categories. We implement a difference-indifferences framework, finding a total effect of $8.66 under mandatory programs, representing 8.2% of average monthly food spending. Separately, we find that voluntary curbside composting programs increase monthly household food expenditures by $3.58, while mandatory programs that require residents to separate organics lead to an additional $5.08 increase. These results indicate a notable rebound effect: while diversion programs reduce landfill emissions, the unaccounted for increase in food demand leads to an estimated $24 billion rise in food loss and waste in the United States alone and nearly $827 million in additional greenhouse gas damages. The findings highlight the need to account for behavioral responses in environmental policy design.

title: Safe Asset Shortage and the Banking Cycle
affiliations: Higher Colleges of Technology

detail.title: Safe Asset Shortage and the Banking Cycle
detail.abstract: The paper examines the role of safe assets as public provision of media of storage in an economy with financial frictions during a banking cycle. In an endowment economy with households that face random consumption needs, banks provide liquidity insurance to subject to a solvencylimited securitization constraint. Banks invest in long-term risky assets and public debt, as public debt is the only safe asset in positive net supply. The dynamic behavior of the economy is studied under two policy regimes: (a) an accommodating regime in which the supply of public debt is allowed to adjust freely to demand; (b) a non-accommodating regime in which the quantity of the public debt is fixed. In the presence of shocks to the economy, a dynamic complementarity between long-term investment and the public debt arises due to the interaction between deposits, investment, and pledgeable returns under a binding constraint. In an accommodating government debt regime, the increase in government debt provides media of storage to satisfy the solvency constraint without rationing deposits. In a non-accommodating regime, with the quantity of government debt fixed, deposits are rationed, investment and pledgeable income falls. The effects of the shortage of safe assets work through model even when the economy is above an effective lower bound of interest rate and the interest rate adjusts to equilibrate the market. The model provides an additional explanation for the observed surge in safe government debt in the aftermath of financial crises. It also provides an alternative view on bank runs, disintermediation and the emergence of financial bubbles.

title: Adding Private Equity to Retirement Savings
affiliations: Stanford Law School

detail.title: Adding Private Equity to Retirement Savings
detail.abstract:
Trillions of dollars are held in private pension trusts and accounts, making these pensions a cornerstone of Americans' individual economic security and America's economic foundations. However, in recent decades, there have been massive changes in the structure of these pensions.
Once centered around "defined benefit" (DB) plans, America's pensions have rapidly shifted toward a system of "defined contribution" (DC) plans such as 401(k)s. And thus far at least, the regulatory framework for DC plans has excluded private equity-a complex, pricey, but also rapidly growing asset class-in all but name.
Yet given recent political developments, including an August 2025 executive order for the Department of Labor to reconsider the laws in this area, discussions around the addition of private equity to DC plans are likely to come to a head sooner rather than later. In contrast to the investments that currently dominate DC plans, private equity offers possibly better returns, but also greater risks.
This Article is the first academic work to comprehensively evaluate private equity in the context of the legal frameworks that govern American DC plans. In particular, this Article makes three contributions. First, this Article explores and analyzes how a complex web of laws and economic incentives shapes the investments used by DC plans and how that web has barred the use of private equity thus far. Second, within that legal and economic context, this Article evaluates the pros and cons of adding private equity to DC plans. Finally, this Article makes policy suggestions to mitigate the worst abuses that private equity might visit upon Americans saving for retirement.

detail.abstract: This study examined the influence of spatial interdependencies on regional total factor productivity in Japan by focusing on the contrasting effects of borrowed size and agglomeration shadows. Using panel data from 47 Japanese prefectures between 2000 and 2018, we compared the manufacturing and non-manufacturing sectors by estimating the Spatial Durbin Model and the Spatial Durbin-SARAR Model. These models enable a detailed decomposition of productivity effects into direct (within region) and indirect (spillover) components across space. The results indicated that industrial agglomeration and transport capital positively influence local productivity in both sectors. However, negative spillovers, interpreted as agglomeration shadow effects, were also observed, where the concentration in neighboring regions suppressed local performance. Human capital exerted a consistently positive impact on manufacturing, with evidence of interregional spillover effects. These findings highlight the sector-specific spatial dynamics and indicate the need for differentiating regional policy responses. For the manufacturing sector, promoting networked industrial clustering and labor mobility can enhance productivity but must be balanced against the risks of overconcentration. In the nonmanufacturing sector, decentralized service economies and spatially equitable infrastructure investments are critical for reducing competitive displacement from urban cores. By clarifying the conditions under which borrowed size and agglomeration shadow effects prevail, this study contributes to spatial productivity theory and offers actionable insights for designing regionally differentiated development strategies.

title: Türkiye's Homemade Crises
affiliations: Bilkent University - Department of Economics and Yale School of Management

detail.title: Türkiye's Homemade Crises

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This article was prepared for the 2025 DNB-Riksbank-Bundesbank-CBI Macroprudential Conference, Amsterdam, June 18--19, 2025.

detail.abstract: Türkiye's response to post-pandemic inflation is a cautionary tale of how political pressure for low interest rates can create macroeconomic instabilities. While central banks worldwide raised interest rates to combat inflation in 2021-2023, Turkish authorities pursued the opposite strategy: cutting real rates to deeply negative levels while implementing financial engineering tools, FX interventions, and financial repression to stabilize markets. The centerpiece was a novel FX-protected deposit scheme (KKM) that guaranteed depositors against currency depreciation, shifting exchange rate risk to the government balance sheet. We provide a detailed account of this policy experiment and develop a theoretical model focusing on how KKM functions and creates vulnerabilities. Our model reveals that pressure to keep interest rates below inflation-targeting levels can lead to an interconnected destabilizing sequence. Low rates generate inflation, current account deficits, and exchange rate depreciation. KKM provides partial stabilization by effectively raising rates for savers while maintaining low rates for borrowers. However, this creates growing contingent fiscal burdens and vulnerability to self-fulfilling currency and sovereign debt crises. This explains additional policies adopted including capital flow management, financial repression, and return to orthodox monetary policy. As central banks worldwide face renewed pressure to set lower policy rates, Türkiye's experience illustrates the consequences.

detail.abstract:
Portuguese Abstract: O retrospecto do mercado de capitais nacional é fundamental para entender os desafios que ele encontra na atualidade, e as características de sua histórica concentração acionária. Essa concentração, por sua vez, gera dinâmicas de conflito entre acionistas controladores e minoritários. O presente estudo parte da hipótese de que a má performance de companhias de capital disperso não está vinculada a falhas no modelo de governança corporativa, mas sim a fatores macroeconômicos e dinâmicas setoriais específicas. Por meio da categorização da estrutura de capital proprietário das 100 maiores companhias da B3 e da análise dos retornos de ações em múltiplos recortes temporais, busca-se desassociar a estrutura de capital proprietário dos resultados de mercado. A proposta é contribuir para o debate sobre poder de controle, estrutura de capital e governança corporativa no Brasil, questionando diagnósticos simplistas sobre a eficácia de modelos de capital disperso.

English Abstract: The history of the Brazilian capital markets is essential for understanding the challenges it currently faces, as well as the characteristics of its traditionally concentrated ownership structure. This concentration, in turn, gives rise to conflicts between majority and minority shareholders. This study is based on the hypothesis that the underperformance of widely held companies is not due to flaws in the corporate governance model, but rather to macroeconomic factors and specific industry dynamics. By categorizing the ownership structures of the 100 largest companies listed on B3 and analyzing stock returns across multiple timeframes, the aim is to decouple ownership structure from market performance. The goal is to contribute to the debate on control power, ownership structure, and corporate governance in Brazil, challenging simplistic assessments of the effectiveness of dispersed ownership models.

publicationDetails.detailsText: ECB Working Paper No. 2025/3133

detail.abstract: This paper contributes to the literature on the price Phillips curve by exploiting subnational regional data from 11 euro area countries. Beyond controlling for aggregate fluctuations common across euro area regions, our approach accounts for country-specific dynamics, including national inflation expectations, thereby addressing key limitations in previous studies. Our results suggest that the Phillips curve in the euro area is relatively flat, but statistically significant. Furthermore, we provide novel evidence on potential nonlinearities in the price Phillips curve and highlight the critical role of properly accounting for country-specific factors such as inflation expectations. These findings provide new insights for the conduct of monetary policy and underscore the value of regional data in euro area macroeconomic analysis.

title: Platform Competition and Strategic Trade-Offs for Complementors: Heterogeneous Reactions to the Entry of a New Platform
affiliations: and ISTO, LMU Munich

detail.title: Platform Competition and Strategic Trade-Offs for Complementors: Heterogeneous Reactions to the Entry of a New Platform
detail.abstract: We study how the entry of a rival platform affects the strategies of the incumbent's complementors. The latter face a trade-off: While the entry threatens their benefits from indirect network effects, it also allows them to escape intense within-platform competition. Studying Epic Games' entry into the PC video game market-until then dominated by Steam-we show that this tradeoff does not resolve uniformly, driving heterogeneity in strategic reactions. Complementors with weaker strategic resources (independent developers) were more likely to multihome but became less responsive to the incumbent's attempts to orchestrate collective action through platform-wide sales promotions. In contrast, complementors more reliant on indirect network effects (multiplayer developers) were less likely to multihome but became more responsive to orchestration attempts.

detail.abstract: Purpose of review: This systematic review aims to map the current landscape of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) applications within economics and finance in sub-Saharan Africa. It seeks to identify dominant research trends, key application domains, model performance, emerging opportunities, and the significant socioeconomic implications of these technologies for the region. Recent findings: Current research demonstrates a significant surge in AI and ML adoption in African economics and finance, particularly since 2017. Key applications include: (1) poverty and economic wellbeing prediction using satellite imagery and alternative data sources, with models explaining over 70% of the variation in village-level wealth; (2) real-time economic nowcasting to track the impacts of major events like the COVID-19 pandemic; and (3) enhancing financial inclusion and risk management through AI-driven credit scoring and fraud detection, where models achieve F1-scores exceeding 0.80. Deep learning (DL) models, especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for geospatial data and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for time-series forecasting, are pivotal. Summary: AI and ML are transforming economics and finance in sub-Saharan Africa by providing scalable, high-frequency, and granular data that bypasses traditional data gaps. These technologies offer transformative potential for evidence-based policymaking, financial stability, and inclusive growth. However, significant challenges persist, including data sparsity, infrastructural limitations, and the risk of algorithmic bias. Future advancements depend on developing localized, context-aware models, investing in data infrastructure, and establishing robust ethical governance frameworks to ensure equitable outcomes.

detail.abstract: This study explores whether wisdom arises from effective dialogue-a question that bridges theology, philosophy, and cognitive science. It examines the epistemic and transformative role of dialogue both in classical religious traditions and in contemporary human-AI interaction. Drawing from Buddhist yonisomanasikāra (wise reflection), Islamic sohbah (sincere companionship), and Christian I-Thou theology (Buber, 1970), this paper argues that true wisdom emerges from dialogical processes rooted in sincerity, attentiveness, and moral intention. In the modern context, this study extends the discussion to artificial intelligence as a "reflective interlocutor," capable of prompting metacognitive awareness through iterative questioning. Using conceptual analysis and comparative interpretation, the paper concludes that dialogue-whether with humans or AI-functions as a mirror of thought. When grounded in reflection and critical inquiry, such dialogue fosters cognitive transformation and self-awareness, but when driven by haste or bias, it produces superficial reasoning and epistemic distortion.

title: Capital Allocation Model (CAM): A Multi-Criteria Framework for Oil & Gas Offshore Project Prioritization

detail.title: Capital Allocation Model (CAM): A Multi-Criteria Framework for Oil & Gas Offshore Project Prioritization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A

publicationDetails.detailsText: Portfolio, Economics, Financial MOdels

detail.abstract: The offshore oil and gas industry faces persistent challenges in capital allocation due to high investment requirements, long development horizons, and elevated technical and financial risks. Conventional evaluation approaches, which rely primarily on Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR), often neglect critical dimensions such as reserve quality, infrastructure interdependence, and portfolio diversification. This narrow perspective has contributed to frequent cost overruns and value erosion in large-scale offshore projects. This paper presents the Capital Allocation Model (CAM), an adaptive MCDM tool that combines financial performance, technical risk, and strategic factors for prioritizing investments. CAM assesses five weighted criteria: NPVsc, EBITDA/CAPEX, CFIR, 1P reserves, and a Technical Risk Score, and applies vector normalization to ensure comparability across heterogeneous KPIs. Strategic orientations (Aggressive Growth, Balanced, Long-Term/Resilience) are operationalized through weight ranges rather than fixed coefficients, aligning rankings with corporate priorities while maintaining auditability. In contrast, the NPV-only approach systematically rewarded projects with high financial returns regardless of risk or reserves, overlooking structural vulnerabilities. CAM provides a more nuanced prioritization: growth-oriented strategies emphasize high-value, high-efficiency projects, whereas resilience-oriented strategies prioritize reserve-rich, lower-risk assets. This adaptability offers executives transparent, scenario-based decision support, enhancing both the defensibility and strategic alignment of capital allocation decisions. CAM's framework is extensible to sectors beyond oil and gas, including renewables, infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing, providing a versatile methodology for investment optimization in uncertain environments. CAM was validated using a simulated portfolio of six offshore projects and benchmarked against a traditional NPV-only ranking. Results demonstrate that CAM not only improves overall portfolio value but also reduces exposure to high-risk assets. Quantitative efficiency metrics confirm its robustness: the Scenario Differentiation Index (SDI) reached 0.72, indicating effective sensitivity to strategic priorities, while the Pareto Efficiency Ratio (PER) was 83%, showing that most top-ranked projects are also non-dominated in efficiency terms. Rank correlations across scenarios (Kendall's τ = 0.68-0.82) further demonstrate a balance between stability and adaptability. To avoid over-interpreting near-ties, we define a practical materiality threshold of ΔScore ≥ 0.02. Rank changes below this gap are labeled "immaterial," ensuring that scenario conclusions reflect meaningful performance differences rather than numerical noise.

detail.abstract: Nigeria government recent economic reforms that sees major shakes up in government policies including major reforms like the removal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rate have reignited the debate among economists and social critics on the appropriate balance between fiscal activism and market discipline to achieve macroeconomic stability. This study draws on economic principles generated during the period of great economic debate in the 1930s to 1940s from foremost economists Maynard Keynes and Friedrich Hayek and their colleagues on how the government should have responded to the great depression that started in America in 1930s and gradually spread throughout the world. Even though their positions were seen by many to be contradictory, some economists believe they were also complimentary. The Keynesian theorists were in favour of countercyclical fiscal interventions to address economic shocks and stimulate aggregate demand while Hayekian theorists highlight market led resource allocation, sensitivity to price signals, institutional discipline and focus on long-term efficiency. The study shows how the Nigeria government can leverage on this debate to reform the economy. Targeted short-term stimulus, protection of price signals, financial transparency, investment in the supply side, and building of formidable institutions are the recommended policy guides.

publicationDetails.detailsText: AGRFORMET-D-25-02514

detail.abstract: Accurate estimation of cropland evapotranspiration (ETc) is critical for irrigation management and efficient water resource utilization, yet remains challenging due to complex surface heterogeneity and human interventions. Land surface temperature-based remote sensing models (LST-ET) have been widely applied at field and regional scales for their strong physical foundations and computational efficiency. However, their performance in agricultural systems is often constrained by structural limitations, prompting the development of diverse improvement strategies. Despite increasing efforts to enhance LST-ET models, few studies to date have systematically synthesized these strategies or quantitatively assessed their effectiveness. To address this gap, a meta-analysis was conducted using 128 datasets extracted from 90 peer-reviewed studies. A unified classification framework of structural improvement strategies was proposed, and model performance before and after modification was evaluated using three metrics: absolute improvement, relative improvement rate, and residual potential utilization rate. Results showed that all strategies improved ETc estimation to varying degrees. Input mechanism enhancements yielded the highest gains in R2, while error reduction (RMSE%) showed no significant differences across strategies. Model accuracy was more influenced by improvement strategies than by environmental conditions. Additionally, initial model performance influenced outcomes, with R2 showing diminishing returns and RMSE% retaining notable room for optimization. Overall, current LST-ET models have yet to achieve optimal performance in cropland regions. Future improvements should aim to reduce systematic biases while enhancing regional adaptability. This work provides insights into the current landscape of LST-ET model improvements and theoretical guidance for their continued development and application in agricultural systems.

detail.title: The Atomistic Fallacy in Political Science and its Implications for How we Study the Far Right: Lessons for the Left and Trade Unions

detail.abstract: Far-right parties have significantly improved their electoral performance in recent years. During the ‘mega election year’ of 2024, these parties made significant electoral gains at the local and national levels. In Germany, for example, the Alternative for Germany (AfD) gained ground in German federal states such as Thuringia and Saxony in September 2024, after the Rassemblement National (RN) had forged ahead in the snap parliamentary election in France a couple of months earlier. The June 2024 European Parliament elections also witnessed the rise of the far right across many – if not most – Member States. These developments follow a decade or more of rising support for far-right parties in every corner of the continent, ranging from the Sweden Democrats and the Finns Party in Scandinavia, through the Dutch Freedom Party (PVV) in the Netherlands and the Austrian Freedom Party (FPÖ), to Vox in Spain and Chega in Portugal. Indeed, it is difficult to find a European country without a successful far-right party. A look at the longer term also reveals a stark picture: far-right parties in Europe have tripled their support since the early 1990s and 2000s (Rooduijn et al. 2024).

title: Intelligent Computing Power Network & Smart City Innovation
affiliations: and Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) - Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS), Graduate School of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Students

detail.title: Intelligent Computing Power Network & Smart City Innovation
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to deeply explore the important role and far-reaching significance of cloud-edge collaborative intelligent computing networks in the development of future cities. From both theoretical and practical perspectives, this study delves into the key role of urban centralized and distributed collaborative artificial intelligence (AI) computing power networks in the development of future cities. Taking Beijing as an example, the study designs an innovative collaborative architecture scheme of "centralized core hub + distributed edge nodes" for AI computing power. It is found that centralized intelligent computing, with its strong computing capability, supports macro applications such as city brains, complex governance models, and largescale industrial upgrading, serving as the core engine for urban economic growth and innovationdriven development. In contrast, decentralized edge intelligent computing, leveraging its advantages of low latency, high privacy, and localized processing, empowers micro applications such as smart homes, personal health monitoring, and real-time traffic management, directly improving residents' quality of life and the real-time response capability of urban operations. The study concludes that cloud-edge collaborative intelligent computing networks represent an inevitable trend to address the complex challenges of modern cities and achieve intelligent upgrading. They not only significantly enhance the efficiency of urban operations and the level of refined governance but also strongly drive the growth of the digital economy, the intelligent upgrading of industries, and the optimization of public services, thereby comprehensively improving residents' quality of life and exerting a profound impact on urban development.

detail.title: Does Awareness Serve as Key Determinant in Making Crop Insurance Decision? A Study in the Context of Hooghly District

detail.abstract: India is an agrarian country where agriculture is heavily influenced by unpredictable nature of the environment. Crop insurance serves as a protective measure for agricultural production, playing a crucial role in stabilizing farmers' incomes. By mitigating risks, it enables farmers to allocate more investments to their agricultural endeavors. The efficacy of crop insurance is closely tied to the number of participants in the program. In developing countries like India, where a significant portion of farmers falls into the marginal category, the crop insurance penetration remains low. This study aims to investigate the relationship between the uptake of crop insurance and awareness levels among farmers. This study is based on primary data collected from Hooghly district of West Bengal in 2023. The logit regression model was employed as the methodology for analysis. The results shows a positive relationship between awareness and the likelihood of farmers opting for crop insurance.

title: Prediction And Analysis on Demand and Supply Using Machine Learning
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Prediction And Analysis on Demand and Supply Using Machine Learning
detail.abstract:
This study investigates the prediction and analysis of demand and supply dynamics for titanium-based products at Kerala Minerals and Metals Ltd. (KMML), India’s leading titanium dioxide producer. The research addresses persistent challenges of demand–supply imbalance, overstocking, and capacity constraints by applying quantitative and machine learning–driven forecasting models, particularly time-series and Prophet techniques. Data spanning 2020 to 2025, complemented by projections for 2026, was analyzed using both primary inputs from industry stakeholders and secondary market sources.

The findings reveal a market trajectory shaped by COVID-19 disruption, rapid recovery, peak demand growth, temporary slowdown due to inventory saturation, and subsequent capacity-constrained expansion. Demand rose from below 2,000 tons per month in 2020 to a structural plateau of 3,500–4,500 tons by 2026, with seasonal peaks in April and October and troughs in December. Forecasts highlight recurring risks of unmet demand as production nears the 4,000-ton monthly ceiling, particularly in 2026 when several months are projected to exceed capacity.

The study concludes that while KMML is well positioned to benefit from strong market fundamentals, its long-term success depends on expanding production capacity, refining demand forecasting, and adopting agile inventory management strategies. By integrating machine learning techniques with industry insights, the research offers a framework for aligning production with market realities, thereby reducing mismatches, mitigating risks, and supporting the company’s competitiveness in a volatile global titanium market.

reference: ETUI Research Paper - Policy Brief 2025.04
title: Time for an Eco-Social Minimum Income Rethinking Welfare for Ecological Transformations
affiliations: European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) and Independent

detail.title: Time for an Eco-Social Minimum Income Rethinking Welfare for Ecological Transformations

publicationDetails.detailsText: ETUI Research Paper - Policy Brief 2025.04
publicationDetails.journalName: European Trade Union Institute (ETUI) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Policy recommendations 
• Recognise the crucial role of social assistance in protecting vulnerable persons and preventing new social risks from arising from climate change and the green transition. 
• Reimagine existing policy frameworks by adapting existing minimum income schemes to address socio-ecological challenges.
 • Redesign minimum income schemes through an eco-social lens, reforming generosity and conditionality, while broadening eligibility criteria. This approach allows minimum income schemes to cover a wider spectrum of the population by responding not only to existing needs (such as poverty or unemployment), but also to new ecological and labour market risks (for example, climate-related displacement, loss of jobs, regional economic decline). 
• Ensure sustainable funding for expanded minimum income schemes through progressive taxation mechanisms aligned with the polluter pays principle, for example, redistributing revenues from carbon taxes or the EU Emissions Trading System. This should ensure adequate financing and fair burden-sharing in the transition.

title: Forecasting Seasonal Time Series with Random Forests

detail.title: Forecasting Seasonal Time Series with Random Forests

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflicts of interest to declare.

detail.abstract: This paper demonstrates that the random forest is a useful tool for forecasting (detrended) seasonal time series. In an extensive simulation study, we evaluate the forecasting performance of the random forest across time series with different seasonal patterns. We then apply the random forest to predict Austrian monthly tourism demand before and after COVID-19. We find that its "classification" ability captures regular seasonal patterns, while its flexibility accommodates irregularities and handles anomalies, such as crisis periods, in the training sample. Additionally, incorporating calendar variables is straightforward and further improves forecasting accuracy. When a traditional model already captures the main seasonal pattern of a time series, the random forest can add value in a two-step approach by modeling local deviations. Finally, in the empirical application, we use Shapley values to provide additional insights on the time-varying contributions of different groups of predictors on the random forest tourism forecasts.

title: A Sovereign Advisory System for Canada: Rebuilding Strategic Foresight in Trade and Innovation
affiliations: New York Law School

detail.title: A Sovereign Advisory System for Canada: Rebuilding Strategic Foresight in Trade and Innovation

declarations.funderStatement: Originally published by The Centre for International Governance Innovation (CIGI) on October 8, 2025

detail.abstract: Canada risks falling behind in trade negotiations without a rebuilt legislated advisory system and new sectoral advisory groups. This article examines Canada's once world-leading trade advisory system, which has been replaced with ad hoc consultations that lack continuity, confidentiality, and technical rigor. This puts the country at a disadvantage compared to its peers, including the United States, where institutionalized advisory systems provide negotiators with structured, sectoral intelligence. Rebuilding a legislated sovereign advisory system that includes new sectoral advisory groups would restore foresight capacity and strengthen Canada's negotiating position in the 2026 CUSMA review. Without such reform, Canada risks entering the renegotiations as a reactive and fragmented entity, while the United States advances with strategic depth and sectoral leverage. The article proposes the establishment of a Canadian Trade and Economic Security Council (CTESC) with a new generation of sectoral advisory groups that cover critical domains, including the digital economy, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, and cloud sovereignty. Appointments should be made with representatives from Canadian-owned firms, provinces, Indigenous governments, labour organizations, and civil society. The proposed system would provide transparency without sacrificing confidentiality, enabling continuous consultation while protecting Canada's negotiating interests.

title: Financial Inclusion in India: A Special Reference to Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana

detail.title: Financial Inclusion in India: A Special Reference to Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana

publicationDetails.detailsText: Financial Sector Reforms in Developing Economies, Page No: 675-688; ISBN NO: 978-81-928721-1-8; 2015

detail.abstract: India is the home of more than 1.2 billion people. Of this mammoth population most of the people live below poverty line and with no banking facilities. Giving all the people an opportunity to be financially literate and have banking opportunity is still a distant dream. The previous Governments as well as the present Government had taken various initiatives to provide banking facilities to these people especially to people living in rural areas. But still, we are far behind the mission of financial inclusion for all. The objectives behind such initiatives are to save the poor people from falling prey to money lenders and ensure social as well as economic upliftment of these people. People can be brought under the fold of organised financial sector by opening more and more branches of bank but opening a brick and mortar branch in every nook and corner of this large country is practically not feasible so the Government adopted other methods like Business Correspondent (BC) and Business Facilitation (BF) models, giving banking license to post offices, relaxing KYC norms and so on the latest being schemes like Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY). This paper aims at throwing light on Financial Inclusion in India, what has been done for financial inclusion, how successful those were and colder be done with special reference to PMJDY.

title: Hospital Charity Care & The Hill-Burton Act

detail.title: Hospital Charity Care & The Hill-Burton Act
detail.abstract: Hospital provision of charity care plays a crucial role in ensuring healthcare access for uninsured and low-income patients, yet the factors influencing this provision remain poorly understood. This paper examines how hospital charity care responds to regulatory changes by analyzing the long-term effects of the Hill-Burton Act of 1946, which allocated $6 billion to over 3,500 hospitals in exchange for those facilities providing free and reduced-cost care to uninsured patients for 20 years. Using detailed hospital financial data from four large states, patient discharge data from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project, and event studies around the expiration of Hill-Burton charity care obligations, I analyze the impact of these regulatory expirations on hospital conduct and patient access to care. I find that Hill-Burton hospitals decrease charity care provision by 30% and reduce admissions of likely charity-eligible patients by 14% after their obligations expire. These patients are subsequently shifted to neighboring public and non-profit hospitals, where they are required to pay for care. While county-level access to hospital care remains stable, county-level charity care spending drops by 20% after the first expiration of Hill-Burton obligations in the county. These results reveal strategic behavior in hospital charity care provision and highlight the importance of considering hospital objectives and responses when designing policies to improve healthcare access for underinsured populations.

title: Seafood Purchasing in Response to Type 2 Diabetes Diagnosis
affiliations: , University of Florida and University of Florida

detail.title: Seafood Purchasing in Response to Type 2 Diabetes Diagnosis
detail.abstract: Disease diagnosis can be a critical turning point in individuals' lives and incentivize them to make lifestyle changes. However, the extent to which these events lead to significant changes in short-and long-term food choices and the extent to which this depends on demographics remain less studied. Seafood is a food group that is particularly interesting in this context. Despite well-documented health benefits, seafood consumption remains below recommended levels and vary significantly between demographic groups. Using a specific food group also allows the use of quantities in addition to expenditure or an index which may be important due to the closer relationship with nutrients, as well as exploring adjustments of the composition of products. Using the NielsenIQ datasets, this study examines how a type 2 diabetes diagnosis affected seafood purchasing behaviors in the United States, using a two-stage difference in difference approach. Our findings show a significant increase in seafood purchases post-diagnosis by 2%; the persistence of the impact vary about 8 years, before the effect eventually declines. There is heterogeneity in the results, showing that demographic differences in households play an important role in seafood purchases responses to a diagnosis, as well seafood species. Of particular interest is the fact that canned seafood was included in the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children in the U.S. in 2024, increasing access to low income households that traditionally are among the groups that consumes least seafood. Our results indicate strong positive responses for canned seafood for low income households.

title: Insider Collusion as a Threat to Property Rights: Experimental Evidence from West Africa
affiliations: Pompeu Fabra University - Department of Economics and Business, University Pompeu Fabra, Department of Business and Economics, Aarhus University and University of Lausanne - School of Economics and Business Administration (HEC-Lausanne)

detail.title: Insider Collusion as a Threat to Property Rights: Experimental Evidence from West Africa

publicationDetails.detailsText: Pompeu Fabra University, Economics and Business Working Paper Series, 1917, September 15.

detail.abstract: We provide causal evidence on how a community's formal institutions and social structure jointly affect the value of its land to outside investors. Using field research and a lab-in-thefield experiment in rural Benin, we show that potential urban investors perceive a higher risk of expropriatory collusion among villagers-and thus invest less-when villages lack formal land records and exhibit strong social tightness. We also find that, although formalizing land rights increases the confidence of outsiders, it does not eliminate their concerns about collusion: outsiders remain wary of investing in villages with a tight social structure even with formal property rights, indicating that local collusion continues to pose a barrier to developing impersonal property markets. Our findings therefore suggest that in addition to facilitating intra-community investment and trade (e.g., by formalizing land ownership), well-designed property institutions should also guarantee the impartial treatment of outsiders.

title: Annulment: Inside the Largest - and Briefest - School District Consolidation in American History
affiliations: University of Memphis - Cecil C. Humphreys School of Law

detail.title: Annulment: Inside the Largest - and Briefest - School District Consolidation in American History
detail.abstract: This paper offers an inside account of the brief consolidation of urban and suburban school districts in Shelby County, Tennessee in the early 2010s. The  author, a professor at the  University of Memphis Cecil C. Humphreys School of Law, played various roles throughout the process, including as a commissioner on the body charged with crafting the plan of consolidation. The paper thus traces the story from the author's perspectives, drawing on his previous work to frame the educational landscape in Memphis consisting of both Memphis City Schools (approx 100,000 students) and Shelby County Schools (approx 50,000 students) to examine the motivations triggering the consolidation of the two districts in 2010, the tensions at issue through the merger process, and the subsequent "de-merger" of districts into a large urban district surrounded by 6 newly-formed suburban districts. The story touches on issues of educational structure, relations between state and local governance, and disparities in education along lines of race and socioeconomic status. It closes with the author's assessment of how things might have been different, offering lessons for other community's confronting similar dynamics both inside and outside of schools.

reference: Open Research Europe, volume 4, 2024[10.12688/openreseurope.18052.1]
title: Applications of Homomorphic Encryption in Secure Computation
affiliations: Kadir Has University, , AAB College, Saints Cyril and Methodius University of Skopje, , AAB College, South-East European University and AAB College

detail.title: Applications of Homomorphic Encryption in Secure Computation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Open Research Europe, volume 4, 2024[10.12688/openreseurope.18052.1]

detail.abstract:
Background: Homomorphic encryption (HE) represents a pivotal innovation in modern cryptography, offering a pathway to secure computation on encrypted data. This paper embarks on a comprehensive exploration of HE's applications, elucidating its transformative potential in bolstering data security and privacy across various domains.

Methods: The research employs a mixed-methods approach to evaluate HE technologies. Quantitatively, it develops realistic datasets simulating healthcare and financial data, assessing HE's performance in encrypted computations. Various encryption schemes are rigorously tested for efficiency and accuracy under different conditions. Qualitatively, insights from expert interviews and case studies of HE implementations provide additional context on practical challenges and strategic benefits.

Results: The simulations and analyses showcase the efficiency, scalability, and security of HE techniques in diverse scenarios. The empirical evidence validates the real-world applicability of HE, demonstrating its versatility and efficacy in secure computation outsourcing, privacy preserving data analysis, and secure multi-party computation.

Conclusions: This research paper highlights the transformative power of homomorphic encryption, advocating for its widespread adoption and integration. By bridging the gap between theoretical understanding and practical implementation, the paper contributes to advancing secure computation practices, addressing contemporary challenges in data security and privacy amidst evolving cybersecurity threats and the increasing ubiquity of sensitive data. In essence, this research serves as a beacon of insight into the future of data confidentiality and integrity, promoting HE as a crucial tool for revolutionizing the landscape of data security and privacy in an interconnected world.

Plain language summary: This research investigates homomorphic encryption (HE), a cutting- edge technology that allows computations to be performed on encrypted data without needing to decrypt it first. This capability is crucial for protecting sensitive information in fields like healthcare and finance, where data privacy is paramount. The study uses a mix of methods: it creates realistic datasets to test HE's performance in handling tasks like arithmetic and statistical analysis under various conditions. Additionally, insights from interviews with experts and real-world case studies shed light on practical challenges and benefits of HE. By combining these approaches, the research aims to provide a comprehensive evaluation of HE's effectiveness in enhancing data security and privacy, informing future developments in cryptographic techniques.

reference: Journal of Economic Psychology, volume 109, 2025[10.1016/j.joep.2025.102830]
title: Keep Them Out Of It! How Information Externalities Affect The Willingness To Sell Personal Data Online
affiliations: University of Marburg, King’s College London - King's Business School and Erasmus University Rotterdam School of Law, Rotterdam Institute of Law and Economics

detail.title: Keep Them Out Of It! How Information Externalities Affect The Willingness To Sell Personal Data Online

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Economic Psychology, volume 109, 2025[10.1016/j.joep.2025.102830]

detail.abstract: When individuals provide their personal data online, they often disregard that this allows learning about others, too. Our large-scale online experiment reveals that individuals are less willing to provide personal data when sharing can compromise others' privacy, entailing personalized price discrimination. Compared to a benchmark without data compromise, individuals' willingness to sell data decreases when others' data is compromised with 50% or 100% probability. By applying two well-studied interventions-peer effects and a social norm focus-we explore ways to mitigate excessive data sharing, laying the ground for policy design. While peer effects, on average, increase individuals' willingness to provide personal data, making people reflect on the appropriate behavior appears to be a promising social nudge to reduce negative externalities.

title: The Effect of Air Pollution on House Prices: Evidence from Beijing’s Second-Hand Housing Market
affiliations: Royal Holloway University of London and University of London - Royal Holloway College

detail.title: The Effect of Air Pollution on House Prices: Evidence from Beijing’s Second-Hand Housing Market
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the impact of air pollution on house prices using transaction-level data from Beijing's second-hand housing market between 2014 and 2020. We use the introduction of China's national Green Factory certification programme as a source of exogenous variation in air pollution. We exploit both the staggered timing of certification and the distance from individual properties to certified factories to construct our instrument. Our two-stage least squares estimates show that air pollution has a significant negative effect on house prices with a price elasticity of -0.1, in contrast to the largely insignificant OLS coefficients. These findings underscore the importance of accounting for endogeneity of air quality when analyzing its effect on property values.

title: Can Bonds Still Diversify Multi-Asset Portfolios? Income versus Duration in Distinct Correlation Regimes
affiliations: BlackRock, Inc and University of California

detail.title: Can Bonds Still Diversify Multi-Asset Portfolios? Income versus Duration in Distinct Correlation Regimes
detail.abstract: We analyze the diversification benefits of fixed-income instruments under time-varying correlations. We estimate monthly, non-overlapping correlations from daily 10-year Treasury bond returns over the period January 1962 to May 2025. With these data, we use a hidden Markov model to identify three distinct correlation regimes-negative, zero, and positive. These regimes are highly persistent and differ in their diversification value depending on the importance of income versus duration as drivers of bond returns. Dynamically altering the mix of multi-asset portfolio allocations based on the most likely correlation regime materially improves returns while controlling risk.

title: Agent-Based Modelling of Distributive Justice: Inequality, Demography, and Policy Regimes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Agent-Based Modelling of Distributive Justice: Inequality, Demography, and Policy Regimes
detail.abstract: This article operationalises distributive-justice doctrines as executable allocators within a stateful agent-based model (ABM) that nests demography, public budgeting, and legal-institutional rules. Nine principles—Utilitarian, Rawlsian, Prioritarian, Sufficientarian, Equality of Opportunity, Capability, Desert, Nozickian, and Nash—are translated into policy regimes and evaluated under shared macro and demographic conditions. The ABM is validated against post-1960 population and Gini series and employed in historically anchored counterfactuals for the United States and China. Floor-raising and capability-building allocators robustly compress inequality while preserving population momentum; minimal-state designs permit higher and more volatile dispersion. Transition mechanics matter: symmetric execution smoothing and gradual ramps avoid artefactual breaks, yielding credible causal attribution to the allocator. Monte Carlo ensembles confirm that, holding technology and resources fixed, the justice rule is the primary driver of distributional paths. Policy implications follow for sequencing welfare reforms and managing regime change.

title: Sustainable by Choice, Contrarian by Habit: How Finance Professionals React to ESG and Volatility.
affiliations: , MBS School of Business, Université Montpellier I and Université de Nice Sophia Antipolis

detail.title: Sustainable by Choice, Contrarian by Habit: How Finance Professionals React to ESG and Volatility.

declarations.ethicsApproval: This research was validated by the ethical committee of the Center of Environmental Economics of Montpellier (University of Montpellier).
declarations.funderStatement: This project received financial support from the Institut Europlace de Finance (IEF/ILB) and University of Montpellier.

detail.abstract: We study how environmental externalities and volatility shocks shape investment behavior in an incentivized experiment. Finance professionals prefer green over neutral and brown assets, while students strongly avoid brown assets but show less consistent preferences. Professionals follow a contrarian strategy, buying after losses, selling after gains, applied uniformly across asset types. These patterns persist when controlling for return expectations. Since participants form similar price beliefs across assets, trading is not driven by asset-specific expectations but reflects a generalized heuristic. Our results show that professionals pursue ESG-oriented allocation while engaging in volatility-driven trading across all asset classes during market shocks.

title: Effects of No Single-Use Plastic Policy on Household's Buying Behavior of Food Products in Bohol, Philippines
affiliations: Visayas State University, Visayas State University, Leyte, Philippines, Visayas State University - Visayas Socio-Economic Research and Data Analytics Center, Visayas Socio-Economic Research and Data Analytics Center, Visayas State University and Visayas State University - Visayas Socio-Economic Research and Data Analytics Center

detail.title: Effects of No Single-Use Plastic Policy on Household's Buying Behavior of Food Products in Bohol, Philippines
detail.abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of no single-use plastic policy on households' buying behavior of food products. The policy was intended to influence consumer behavior and increase awareness on environmental sustainability but consumers have differing perceptions. This study sought aims to compare the generated household waste in the municipality with and without the No Single-use Plastic policy and identify the factors affecting household's buying behavior of food products amidst policy implementation. Multiple linear and ordinal logistic regression was used to determine the factors that affect households' buying behavior of food products. The study findings revealed that respondents from the municipality without the policy are more likely to purchase more frequently than the respondents from the municipality with the policy. Findings revealed that respondents from the municipality with the policy are less likely to consume single-use plastics providing evidence that the policy was able to reduce single use plastics.

title: From Situational Rhetoric to Systemic Reality: Alliance Dynamics and Economic Restructuring in the Post-Hegemonic Era
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: From Situational Rhetoric to Systemic Reality: Alliance Dynamics and Economic Restructuring in the Post-Hegemonic Era
detail.abstract: This study introduces the concept of "situational clamoring" to explain how defensive political rhetoric triggers rapid alliance deterioration in economically interdependent relationships. We define situational clamoring as defensive independence statements made by leaders under ally pressure. While such rhetoric appears contextual, it creates cascading economic realignments. We test this framework using Netanyahu's 2024-2025 statements and subsequent global responses. Spain canceled $1.35 billion in defense contracts following Netanyahu's "stand alone" declaration. His "Super-Sparta" economic model accelerated European distancing. These patterns validate our theoretical predictions. The findings show that in financially interdependent alliances, rhetorical events function as reliability signals. Partners rationally reassess economic vulnerabilities and seek alternatives. This creates selfreinforcing cycles of partnership deterioration. Our framework bridges political communication and alliance theory, explaining contemporary alliance fragmentation through the interaction of rhetoric and economic interdependence.

title: Understanding Credit Demand: Exploring the Impact of Leverage and Return on Borrowing
affiliations: University of Glasgow, Ametis Institute, Ametis Institute and London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Understanding Credit Demand: Exploring the Impact of Leverage and Return on Borrowing

contentType.other: Under Review in Journal of Economic Surveys

detail.abstract: This study presents a conceptual framework for analyzing the relationship between firm returns and credit demand. By examining the conditional distributions of return on borrowing and leverage, the framework investigates how changes in interest rates and the maximum leverage provision impact credit demand. The study emphasizes the role of the mean and standard deviation of these distributions and introduces the concept of elasticity to quantify the responsiveness of credit demand. The findings provide valuable insights for policymakers in understanding the dynamics of credit demand and formulating effective economic policies. The framework offers a useful tool to assess the implications of interest rate and leverage provision changes on credit demand and support sustainable economic growth in the credit market.

title: Reforming America's High-Skilled Immigration: Evidence-Based Policy for Global Competitiveness
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: Reforming America's High-Skilled Immigration: Evidence-Based Policy for Global Competitiveness

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial, professional, or personal interests that could appear to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors

detail.abstract: The United States faces mounting competitive pressure in global talent markets due to structural deficiencies in its high-skilled immigration system. This study examines the H-1B visa program's performance against domestic workforce challenges and international alternatives, revealing systematic disadvantages that undermine American competitiveness. Using comparative analysis of immigration systems in Canada, Australia, Germany, and Singapore, alongside empirical data on program outcomes, this research demonstrates that lottery-based allocation, processing uncertainty, and unclear permanent residency pathways drive qualified candidates to competitor nations. The analysis proposes evidence-based reforms including merit-based allocation, strategic government oversight, accelerated permanent residency pathways, and regional distribution mechanisms. These recommendations address domestic workforce development concerns while enhancing America's ability to attract and retain global talent.

title: Iranian Turks in the Triangle of Ecology, Demography, and Security: Strategic Implications for Türkiye
affiliations: Istanbul Topkapi University and Association of Digital Ecosystem Governance and Development Research

detail.title: Iranian Turks in the Triangle of Ecology, Demography, and Security: Strategic Implications for Türkiye
detail.abstract: This study examines the geopolitical significance of the approximately 39-40 million Turkish population in Iran, alongside issues of water scarcity and allegations of environmental-demographic engineering, and their implications for Türkiye. Despite Iran's vast energy and mineral resources, international sanctions limit their effective utilization. Meanwhile, nuclear-related international pressures, alarmingly low reservoir levels in Tehran (around 7% capacity), the drying of Lake Urmia, and the reported settlement of PKK/PEJAK elements in Turkish-populated areas generate vulnerabilities that affect not only Iran's internal stability but also Türkiye's border security and ecological sustainability. The study evaluates these vulnerabilities within the ecology-demography-security nexus, situating them in the context of the "Pax Israelica" claim, and offers short-, medium-, and long-term policy recommendations for Türkiye. A central point underscored is that, for the sake of regional stability, Iran's territorial integrity is defended and respected. Findings suggest that the Turkish presence in Iran constitutes not only a socio-cultural reality but also a geopolitical and security factor at the core of Türkiye's strategic vision.

title: Transgender Economics
affiliations: Southern Oregon University, Unaffiliated Author, Bahcesehir University, Sinop University, RAND Corporation and University of Melbourne

detail.title: Transgender Economics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors do not declare any personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced their study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews the state of transgender economic research and labor market data, compiling global data on transgender labor market outcomes, representing half a million transgender individuals across 88 countries between 2005 and 2025, with broad geographic coverage outside of the Middle East and North Africa. Transgender workers, on average, earn just 79.4 cents for every dollar earned by cisgender workers. Transgender workers face twice the unemployment rate of cisgender workers (16.3% vs. 8.0%), despite similar labor force participation rates (63.1% vs. 65.9%), leading to a far lower employment rate (53.1% vs. 60.8%). To explain these findings, we provide the first economic model of gender. The model treats gender as a constrained choice: individuals derive utility from expressing their gender identity but must allocate resources to modify their gender expression, creating a tradeoff. If a person's gender expression deviates from social norms tied to their perceived gender, they may face discrimination, reducing their identity payoff. Consequently, individuals must balance the benefits of expressing their gender identity against the costs of discrimination, minority stress, gender dysphoria, and resources. The model predicts key findings in the literature, such as disparities in mental health and labor market outcomes for transgender individuals, the nonlinear effects of gender transitions, the positive impact of gender-affirming care and supportive family environments on mental health, and the negative effects of perceived gender incongruence, conversion therapy, and identity development in unsupportive families.

title: Challenges in Identifying Factors which Determine the Placement of Children in Care? An International Review
affiliations: University of Reading - ICMA Centre and University of Southampton

detail.title: Challenges in Identifying Factors which Determine the Placement of Children in Care? An International Review
detail.abstract:
Placing a child in out-of-home care is one of the most important decisions made by professionals in
the child care system, with substantial social, psychological, educational, medical and economic
consequences. This paper considers the challenges and difficulties of building statistical models of
this decision by reviewing the available international evidence. Despite the large number of empirical
investigations over a fifty year period, a consensus on the variables associated with this decision is
hard to identify. In addition, the individual models have low explanatory and predictive power and
should not be relied on to make placement decisions. A number of reasons for this poor performance
are offered, and some ways forwards suggested. This paper also aims to facilitate the emergence of
a coherent and integrated international literature from the disconnected and fragmented empirical
studies. Rather than one placement problem, there are many slightly different problems, and therefore
it is expected that a number of related sub-literatures will emerge, each concentrating on a particular
definition of the placement problem.

title: Support Link Formation in Contests: Theory and an Experiment
affiliations: National Research University Higher School of Economics (Moscow), , University of Rome Tor Vergata and National Research University – Higher School of Economics (HSE University)

detail.title: Support Link Formation in Contests: Theory and an Experiment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no relevant or material financial interests that relate to the research described in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: Anastasia Antsygina and Mariya Teteryatnikova acknowledge financial support from the RSF grant No. 24-28-00608.

detail.abstract: Many competitive environments allow for a third party to be indirectly involved by supporting one or both sides in the conflict. Such support can come from trade partners, colleagues, or allies, who can in turn benefit from a supported party's success. We use theory and an experiment to investigate how support relationships develop endogenously in view of a future contest, and how those relationships affect contestant investment. We introduce a two-stage game, in which two competing players have an opportunity to form support links with a third, indirectly involved player before proceeding to the contest stage. We fully characterize conditions under which players have incentives to form support links and how the structure of the support network affects investments in the contest. In a laboratory experiment we find partial support for the theory, however we find patterns of over-investment relative to equilibrium predictions that cannot be explained by standard behavioural phenomena such as "joy of winning" and reciprocity. More precisely, subjects invest more when supported, whether or not their competitor is likewise supported.

title: Strategies, Beliefs, and Social Preferences in the Infinitely Repeated Prisoner's Dilemma
affiliations: Yangzhou University and University of Birmingham

detail.title: Strategies, Beliefs, and Social Preferences in the Infinitely Repeated Prisoner's Dilemma

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study was approved by the Ethics Committee at the University of Birmingham.

detail.abstract: We study how strategies, beliefs, and individual preferences shape cooperation in the infinitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma. In a laboratory experiment, participants play a series of supergames with a systematically varying payoff matrix. Consistent with previous results for one-shot games, we find that temptation reduces cooperation, efficiency increases it, and risk does not affect cooperation rates. Using strategy-frequency estimation, we find that Always Defect, Grim Trigger, Exploitative Grim, and Tit-for-Tat explain group behavior, with payoff changes affecting strategy use. Leveraging the payoff variability and within-participant design for structural model estimation, we find substantial across-participant heterogeneity displaying other-regarding preferences, belief updating, and reciprocity.

title: The Conditional Recognition of Palestine: Middle-Power Assertion and the Erosion of American Diplomatic Hegemony
affiliations: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology

detail.title: The Conditional Recognition of Palestine: Middle-Power Assertion and the Erosion of American Diplomatic Hegemony
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the diplomatic significance of unilateral recognitions of Palestinian statehood by middle powers, using Australia's 2025 announcement as a critical case study. Through a mixed-methods approach combining discourse analysis, diplomatic history, and international relations theory, it argues that these acts represent a profound shift in the structure of the post-Cold War international order, moving from unipolar American hegemony toward a fragmented and multipolar system. The paper introduces the concept of "conditional recognition" as a strategic diplomatic tool that allows states to garner domestic and international moral credibility while avoiding substantive political or economic costs. By examining the breakdown of the Five Eyes consensus and the calculated nature of these recognitions, this research concludes that such moves are less about achieving Palestinian self-determination and more about middle powers asserting independent foreign policy in a changing global landscape. The findings suggest that these recognitions signal not only the decline of American authority to set diplomatic agendas but also the emergence of a new form of performative diplomacy that privileges symbolic action over material change.

title: (Generative) AI in Production Economy
affiliations: University of Chicago - Becker Friedman Institute for Economics and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: (Generative) AI in Production Economy
detail.abstract: We propose a novel static, task-based model, in which generative AI enters as a probabilistic substitute for human labor at the task level. This formulation introduces dual channels – an intensive quality improvement (through better AI performance) and an extensive quantity expansion (via cost-driven AI adoption) – which together rationalize recent empirical patterns in labor demand, firm valuations, and market structure. We then extend the model into a dynamic setting that incorporates deep uncertainty about AI alignment (e.g., existential risk). The dynamic extension derives the socially optimal allocation of resources between AI research (quality innovation), AI deployment (automation capital), and traditional capital. Under greater concern for misalignment risk, the planner optimally reins in AI investment – cutting back on both AI research and AI deployment – even when static productivity gains from AI are large.

detail.abstract: This conceptual paper proposes the AI Value Reflection Hypothesis (AVRH)-a framework for understanding how artificial intelligence (AI) acts as a reflective mirror that amplifies or limits human potential based on users' values, cognitive structures, and learning attitudes. While much literature in AI ethics and human-AI interaction emphasizes algorithmic bias (Crawford, 2021; Binns, 2018; Rahwan et al., 2019), the internal human mechanisms of growth remain underexplored. This paper argues that self-awareness and growth mindset are decisive in determining whether AI becomes a tool for intellectual stagnation or a catalyst for cognitive expansion. Drawing from transformative learning theory (Mezirow, 1991), constructivist epistemology (Piaget, 1970), and human-centered AI ethics (Floridi, 2018; UNESCO, 2021), it suggests that the key process behind human-AI co-learning is cognitive dissonance-the mental tension that arises when AI challenges a person's belief framework. Empirical studies in Computers in Human Behavior (Stadler et al., 2024) and Smart Learning Environments (Zhai et al., 2024) show that over-reliance on AI for confirmatory reasoning reduces critical thinking and adaptability, whereas reflective engagement enhances meta-cognition and learning outcomes. This paper concludes that the ethical and cognitive responsibility for AI use lies not only in system design but also in epistemic responsibility-the willingness to be challenged by one's own reflection through AI. True potential growth arises not from data accumulation, but from dialogue with uncertainty.

detail.title: Efficiency and Resilience: Municipal Welfare Service Management in the Face of the COVID-19 Challenge
detail.abstract: The 2030 Agenda aims to reduce social inequalities, and to achieve this, it is essential to ensure an equitable distribution of resources and to implement a social protection system so, it is necessary to assess whether this system is efficient or not. In the context of local governments, this protection system is developed through the provision of various welfare services. Therefore, it is essential to understand the vulnerabilities of this social protection umbrella and to prevent disruptive events, such as COVID-19, from significantly altering it. Specifically, using the global Malmquist-Luenberger index, we assess the evolution of the efficiency of welfare services in Spain over the period 2015-2021, considering the presence of undesirable outputs. So, we incorporate the evaluation of the degree of municipal progress in the fulfilment of certain SDGs related to the social sphere, such as the reduction of hunger or gender inequality. The results show that COVID-19 exacerbated pre-existing disparities, especially affecting the most vulnerable groups and highlighting the need to strengthen these systems. In addition, in a second-stage truncated regression analysis we identify which variables such as household size, income, female representation or political concentration affect the efficiency levels achieved.

keywords: theory of firm JEL Classifications: D230

detail.abstract: This essay explores the economics of contracting in firms and the role accounting plays in it. It builds on the Coase (1937) insight that firms exist due to contracting-cost advantages over markets. Firms are created when entrepreneurs discover and create a unique domain for repetitive intermediating between factor owners and consumers. It proposes that common accounting methods are a source of that advantage: that they are "contacting-useful." This perspective provides economic rationales for accountants taking a transactional rather than holistic view of firms, for accrual accounting, for cost-based accounting depreciation and for overhead allocation, among other methods. Decision-usefulness theory-the prevailing thesis that the function of accounting is to assist users in deciding among alternative actions-fails to explain the existence of these methods.

title: Climate Risk and Tax-Motivated Outbound Income Shifting
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance, Penn State Harrisburg, Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance and Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: Climate Risk and Tax-Motivated Outbound Income Shifting
detail.abstract: This paper examines the association between climate risk faced by subsidiaries of U.S. multinational corporations (MNCs) and tax-motivated outbound income shifting. We find that higher climate risk in subsidiary countries is associated with lower levels of outbound income shifting by U.S. MNCs. This finding is corroborated by a subsidiary-level analysis based on major weather-related disasters. Cross-sectional tests suggest that the observed association is primarily driven by physical and regulatory risks associated with climate change. The association is intensified by firms' susceptibility and awareness of climate risk, but is moderated by the intensity of intangibles and cost-structure rigidity. Overall, our findings reveal a novel environmental constraint on multinational tax planning and provide new insights into the tax consequences of climate-related risks.

title: Pro-Competition Regulation: Lessons from the Telecoms Sector for Digital Platforms
affiliations: London School of Economics and Independent

detail.title: Pro-Competition Regulation: Lessons from the Telecoms Sector for Digital Platforms
detail.abstract: This paper addresses different ways of addressing the control of market power by major global digital platforms. It does so by comparing the approach taken in the USA, which involves reliance on competition law (including breakups), and the approach in the European Union, where sector-specific legislation in the form of the 2022 Digital Markets Act is employed,. The question is framed as a choice between competition law and a mode of pro-competition regulation in the form of mandated sharing, which requires the dominant firm to share some of its assets with competitors. The assumed goals of the process are to protect direct customers of the dominant firm, and to prevent it from extending its power up or down the value chain (or ecosystem) by self-preference. The main discussion is preceded by a comparison of the parallel case of telecommunications in the period from 1980, comparing the USA's breakup strategy with EU's mandated sharing or unbundling one. The paper then examines the competition law cases currently in progress in the USA, which, if proven, may use breakup or equivalent as a chief remedy. While recognising the uncertainties of the current situation, it suggests that this approach will be protracted, incomplete, and of uncertain outcome. It argues that in the EU a combination of the institutional framework for enforcement and mandated sharing or interoperability available under the DMA is likely to be more productive in achieving the stated objectives.

title: A New Path to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI)

detail.title: A New Path to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI)
detail.abstract: Although current AI systems perform excellently in specific domains, they still lag far behind human intelligence. The future development goal of the artificial intelligence industry is to create machines that can "think" like humans-Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). AGI can not only accomplish predefined tasks but also independently learn, reason, innovate, and even possess self-awareness and values. This is not a simple technological upgrade but a philosophical revolution concerning the "essence of intelligence". We believe that by deeply simulating human physical structure and social behaviors, we can gradually overcome the four core challenges faced by AGI. Through the interaction between humanoid robots and the physical world, and by drawing on the principle of brain neuroplasticity, AGI will acquire cross-domain and multi-modal general knowledge capabilities. By "participating in practice" in the real world and leveraging the bridge of "oracles" and embodied intelligence, AGI will forge genuine cognitive and reasoning abilities that go beyond data patterns. By imitating the "interest-driven" cultivation model of children and utilizing metalearning and knowledge transfer, AGI will unleash the initiative for independent exploration and the creativity to "draw inferences from one instance". By constructing a self-reference frame, autobiographical memory, and an emotional decision-making system, and under the guidance of positive data and constraints of ethical bottom lines, AGI may form healthy selfawareness and correct values. For humans, building AGI is a one-way journey to the future with no turning back. Innovators in this industry need not only superb technical capabilities but also profound philosophical and ethical cognition, a broad humanistic and historical perspective, and noble moral values.

title: Automatic Order, Bandwidth Selection and Flaws of Eigen Adjustment in HAC Estimation
affiliations: and New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business

detail.title: Automatic Order, Bandwidth Selection and Flaws of Eigen Adjustment in HAC Estimation
detail.abstract: In this paper, we propose a new heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent covariance matrix estimator based on the prewhitened kernel estimator and a localized leave-one-out frequency domain cross-validation (FDCV). We adapt the cross-validated log likelihood (CVLL) function to simultaneously select the order of the prewhitening vector autoregression (VAR) and the bandwidth. The prewhitening VAR is estimated by the Burg method without eigen adjustment as we find the eigen adjustment rule of Andrews and Monahan (1992) can be triggered unnecessarily and harmfully when regressors have nonzero mean. Through Monte Carlo simulations and three empirical examples, we illustrate the flaws of eigen adjustment and the reliability of our method.

title: Smooth Tests for Normality in ANOVA
affiliations: , Peking University - Guanghua School of Management and

detail.title: Smooth Tests for Normality in ANOVA
detail.abstract: The normality assumption for random errors is fundamental in the analysis of variance (ANOVA) models, yet it is rarely formally tested in practice. In this paper, we propose Neyman's smooth tests for assessing the normality assumption across various types of ANOVA models. The proposed test statistics are constructed based on the Gaussian probability integral transformation of ANOVA residuals. Under the null hypothesis of normality, the test statistics are asymptotically Chi-square distributed, with degrees of freedom determined by the dimension of the smooth model (the number of orthonormal functions). A data-driven selection of the model dimension using a modified Schwarz's criterion is also discussed. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.
